title: ASG asked the state to seat a student on the higher education council
body: Resolution 79-6, dated 25 September 1979, called for a student representative to be included on the Kentucky Council on Higher Education. It is the earliest dated piece of legislation held for the 1979-80 session in SGA's own archive, and it set the tone of a year in which the organisation, stripped of its entertainment budget, turned to academic and state-level questions.

src.label: SGA Resolution 79-6, Student on Council of Higher Education

title: ASG announced it would run student opinion polls
body: The Herald of 4 October 1979 carried a notice that Associated Student Government opinion polls were planned. This is the announcement, not a report of any poll: it proves what was set up, not what came back. The polls became the signature project of Jamie Hargrove's term, run by a committee under Kevin Kinne, and by the following September the Herald was reporting the first results.

title: ASG proposed cutting special benefits for athletes
body: Ken Morris reported that an ASG proposal would reduce special benefits for athletes. The same issue carried the report by Morris and Tim Fish that favouritism had been alleged in the plans for the Homecoming dance, and news that Western had been denied construction funds.

title: The Homecoming edition ran a history of student government
body: Tom Beshear wrote a feature for the Homecoming edition under the line that student government had grown as the university expanded. It ran in an issue given over to campus history, alongside pieces on Hugh Poland, on how the Second World War left Western with few men, on the naming of the Herald and the Talisman, and on the old Fort Bridge.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Homecoming edition, 25 October 1979

title: A $250 grant to a fraternity drew charges of favouritism
body: Low attendance at the Saturday night Homecoming dance left the sponsoring fraternity, Sigma Chi, out of pocket, and the University Center Board gave the group $250. The Talisman reported that the payment prompted allegations of favouritism because ASG president Jamie Hargrove sat on the centre board and was a former Sigma Chi president. The Herald had already reported on 18 October that favouritism was alleged in the plans for the dance. The yearbook records the allegation only: it names no complainant, reports no finding, and no resolution of the matter appears in the digitised index.

title: A resignation was clarified in the Herald
body: Lisa Hunn wrote to the Herald under the heading that a resignation from the Associated Student Government had been clarified. The digitised index records the letter and its subject but names nobody, so who resigned and why is not established here.

title: A library book drop for Downing University Center
body: Resolution 79-12, dated 13 November 1979, asked for a library book drop to be installed in the Downing University Center so students would not have to walk to the library to return books. It was one of four resolutions filed that night, with the scholarship staffing resolution 79-10 and the part-time activity fee resolution 79-11. ASG asked again two years later, in Resolution 81-4 of September 1981.

src.label: SGA Resolution 79-12, Book Drop in Downing University Center

title: ASG asked for an ice skating rink
body: Resolution 79-13, dated 13 November 1979, asked the university to build a skating rink. SGA's archive holds the document and describes it in a single line, and the Herald of 7 February 1980 carried an item on an ice skating rink. Nothing in the record says the rink was ever built.

title: ASG asked that Keen Hall be made a coed dorm
body: Karen Owen reported that ASG wanted Keen Hall turned into a coed dormitory. The request is Resolution 79-9, dated 30 October 1979 in SGA's own archive under the title Keen Hall Conversion. It came in the same autumn in which the congress refused to back closing Diddle Hall, and coed housing did not reach the Board of Regents until February 1984.

title: Hargrove said ASG had laid foundations
body: Michele Wood reported Jamie Hargrove's assessment at the halfway point of his term, that the Associated Student Government had laid foundations. The same issue reported that open house hours had been increased to 31 a week, the policy question ASG had spent the autumn surveying other universities about.

title: ASG backed the Uniform Landlord Tenant Reform Act
body: Resolution 79-16, dated 5 February 1980 and filed under the name Ultra Extension Support, put ASG behind the Uniform Landlord Tenant Reform Act. Michele Wood reported ASG's support for the tenants' rights bill in the Herald of 7 February, in an issue that also carried a letter from Marion Tabor crediting ASG for its survey work. Off-campus housing stayed on the agenda into the next session, when Resolution 80-34 set out the duties of ASG's off-campus representatives in landlord and tenant disputes.

title: ASG moved to create a vice president for public affairs
body: Resolution 79-18, dated 26 February 1980, supported amending the ASG constitution to add a vice president of public affairs. It failed within a fortnight: on 13 March Michele Wood reported that the proposal for a new congress position had been rejected. The office was still unsettled the following autumn, when Resolution 80-14 of 21 October 1980 carried the same title again.

src.label: SGA Resolution 79-18, Public Affairs Vice President

title: A bill would have changed the activities officer's duties
body: Michele Wood reported a bill to change the duties of the ASG activities officer, and two days later the Herald reported the activities office ready for change. The office was the last remnant of the entertainment function the Board of Regents had moved to the University Center Board the previous spring, taking between $60,000 and $70,000 of ASG's budget with it.

title: The student seat on the state council was refused
body: Michele Wood reported that a student seat on the Council on Higher Education had been denied. It was the answer to Resolution 79-6, which ASG had passed on 25 September 1979 asking for exactly that. The same issue reported that few tickets remained for the NCAA tournament.

title: ASG wrote rules for campaign spending, and for withdrawals
body: Resolution 79-22, dated 8 April 1980, dealt with campaign budgets for ASG elections, and the same night's Resolution 79-23 addressed withdrawal periods and deficiency reports. The spending cap became a live argument the following year, when the congress voted in September 1981 to raise it.

title: ASG proposed a longer period for dropping classes
body: Michele Wood reported that ASG had proposed lengthening the time students had to drop a class. It ran in the same issue that named Steve Fuller, David Rue and Tim Irons as the three candidates for the presidency.

title: The Herald called the centre board seat a burden on ASG
body: The Herald's editorial page argued that the University Center Board position was a burden for the Associated Student Government, and Roland Gibbons drew a cartoon of the centre board against ASG in the same issue. ASG had lost campus entertainment to the centre board the previous spring but its president still sat on it, which was what had made the Homecoming dance grant so awkward.

title: ASG printed a candidate pamphlet for the spring election
body: After the primary, ASG distributed pamphlets carrying a photograph of each executive office candidate and a short statement written by the candidate on their qualifications and plans. President Jamie Hargrove said ASG was moving away from leaving publicity to the candidates and treating turnout as its own responsibility. Rules and elections committee chairman Tim Irons said voters had stayed away in the past because ASG had not told them where the voting tables were or how to use them. The Talisman does not give the exact date the pamphlets went out; the primary was on 17 April and the general election on 24 April.

title: Hargrove went to the White House to meet President Carter
body: ASG president Jamie Hargrove was invited, with about 250 other student leaders, to the White House to discuss foreign and domestic issues with President Jimmy Carter. Hargrove told the Talisman that draft registration and energy policy were the main subjects of his meetings with Carter and some of his senior advisers, and that the purpose of the meeting was to explain why the administration was taking the actions it was taking. The yearbook does not give the date of the visit.

title: ASG surveyed 28 universities on open house hours
body: ASG surveyed 28 institutions comparable to Western and found that Western's open house policy gave the fewest visitation hours per semester of any of them. The Herald reported the finding on 27 September 1979 under the line that Western came last in a 28-college housing poll. ASG also published the results of the previous spring's open house referendum, which showed a majority of students surveyed wanted weekly open houses. The policy finally adopted came from the student affairs office rather than from ASG.

title: The first resolution against room inspections
body: Resolution 80-1, dated 6 May 1980, was a resolution to stop room inspections. It opens the fight that dominated the next academic year, in which ASG twice voted down bills to abolish the inspections, the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union took the question towards a federal court, and the congress instead approved stricter rules for entering rooms.

src.label: SGA Resolution 80-1, Permission for Room Inspection

title: The ASG president also held the student regent seat
body: The 1980 Talisman's account of the Board of Regents records that ASG president Steve Fuller was also sworn in as student regent, in the same passage reporting the board's budget, two regent appointments and $66,000 of university money for renovating the president's home. The two offices were separated during the next session: after Marcel Bush resigned in January 1982 the seat went to a campus-wide election, and Sandra Norfleet won the runoff in February 1982.

title: Fuller opened the year wanting a stronger voice in policy
body: Diane Comer reported in the Herald's back-to-school issue that the Associated Student Government wanted a stronger voice in policy making. It was the opening statement of Steve Fuller's term, and within a fortnight the congress was in the middle of the room inspection fight that ran to Christmas.

title: ASG asked for longer check cashing hours
body: Resolution 80-6, dated 16 September 1980, requested extended hours for the university's check cashing service. It was filed the same night as Resolution 80-5 on open house visitor lists, at the start of a session whose legislation was dominated by residence hall questions.

title: A survey found students uninformed about ASG
body: Diane Comer reported the student opinion poll committee's first survey under the line that students were uninformed about the Associated Student Government. The Talisman gives the numbers: 29 per cent said they would recognise ASG president Steve Fuller, 31 per cent said they would recognise university centre director Ron Beck, and 28 per cent thought Beck was the ASG president. Seventy-four per cent said they would recognise university president Donald Zacharias. Committee chairman Kevin Kinne said he was disappointed so few could tell Fuller and Beck apart and more surprised that a quarter did not know Zacharias.

title: ASG objected to how residence hall budget cuts were shared out
body: Resolution 80-7, dated 18 September 1980, concerned what ASG called the inequity of the cuts made to residence hall budgets. Money was tight across the university that autumn, and the congress returned to the theme in April 1981 with Resolution 81-1, recording its dissatisfaction with budget cuts generally.

title: ASG made its own officers keep office hours
body: Resolution 80-9, dated 22 September 1980, required ASG officers to hold office hours and to report their availability. It is one of the few pieces of legislation from the session aimed at the organisation itself rather than at the university.

title: Dean Keown criticised a resolution and members walked out before the vote
body: Diane Comer reported that Charles Keown, the dean of student affairs, criticised an ASG resolution and that members left the meeting before the vote was taken. The same issue reported that advance registration would be extended to all students. Keown stayed a critic of ASG's internal changes and publicly questioned the organisation's constitutional revisions again in March 1983.

title: Low attendance at its own meetings disappointed the president
body: Diane Comer reported that the Associated Student Government's low attendance had disappointed president Steve Fuller. The same issue reported that students would grade faculty performance and carried a piece on how the room inspections left hall directors in the middle.

title: ASG refused to destroy the open house visitor list
body: Diane Comer reported that ASG rejected a bill to destroy the open house list. The congress had filed Resolution 80-5 on open house visitor lists three weeks earlier, and returned to visitor lists again in Resolution 80-30 the following March. The privacy of those lists sat alongside the room inspection fight as the year's running argument about what the university could record about students.

title: A joint resolution with Interhall Council on restroom stall doors
body: Resolution 80-10, dated 14 October 1980, was a joint resolution of the Interhall Council and ASG asking for stall doors to be installed in residence hall restrooms. Joint work with Interhall Council ran on through the decade, from this to the shared coed housing poll of September 1982.

title: ASG endorsed a rape prevention measure
body: Diane Comer reported that the Associated Student Government had endorsed a rape prevention measure. Ten days earlier the congress had filed Resolution 80-11 under the title Coed Security. The same issue reported that the dormitory inspections would be argued in court and carried an editorial saying inspections should stop until a ruling came.

title: ASG asked for the Downing grill to open on Sundays
body: Resolution 80-19, dated 18 November 1980, requested that the Downing University Center grill open on Sundays and holidays. It was filed the same night as Resolution 80-18 on advanced registration.

src.label: SGA Resolution 80-19, Downing University Center Grill & Cafeteria

title: The Herald said inactivity had improved ASG's image
body: The Herald's editorial page argued that the Associated Student Government's image was improved by inactivity, and ran a cartoon of an ASG clown in the same issue. A week later Marcel Bush, then a member and the following year's president, wrote in to defend the organisation.

title: ASG approved the stricter room entry rules
body: Diane Comer reported that the Associated Student Government had approved stricter rules for entering student rooms, a fortnight after the bill was introduced. The bill set out more standardised procedures for inspections and maintenance than the Hilltopics handbook gave, and was ASG's answer to a semester in which it had twice refused to call for the inspections to be abolished. The same issue carried a letter from member Lonnie Sears saying ASG wanted feedback.

title: ASG passed a resolution backing President Zacharias
body: The Herald reported an Associated Student Government resolution backing the university president, in an issue reporting Donald Zacharias meeting a state panel over money and a student sharing his budget worries. The paper reported on 10 February that students would sponsor a rally to back Zack, and on 12 February that about 200 people had gathered for it. The Herald's index does not say ASG organised the rally, only that it had passed the resolution.
money: about 200 at the rally two weeks later

title: ASG put off action on the open house bill
body: Robert Pillow reported that the Associated Student Government had postponed action on the open house bill. A week later he reported the congress conducting a survey of its own on inspections, and by 26 February committee absentees were delaying ASG action altogether.

title: ASG asked for video game machines in the residence halls
body: Resolution 80-28, dated 10 March 1981, requested that electronic video game machines be placed in residence halls. It belongs to a run of small quality-of-life measures that spring, alongside resolutions on ice machines, change machines and painting.

title: Only one polling place was opened for the ASG election
body: Robert Pillow reported that one poll would be open for the Associated Student Government elections. Five days later he reported four candidates getting a surprise, and the Herald's editorial page ran a piece saying few candidates would have to sweat out the result. After the vote Pillow wrote a column headed Who Cares, arguing the election would win no award for organisation.

title: Off-campus representatives given a role in landlord disputes
body: Resolution 80-34, dated 31 March 1981, set out the duties of ASG's off-campus housing representatives in landlord and tenant disputes. It followed the previous session's Resolution 79-16, which had put ASG behind the Uniform Landlord Tenant Reform Act.

title: The new administration was sworn in as the Herald counted the cost
body: The Herald reported the new Associated Student Government administration sworn in, alongside Robert Pillow's column headed Who Cares, which argued the election would not win an award for organisation, and a Bloss editorial cartoon on ASG. Marcel Bush had beaten David Sturgeon the week before, after recounts in the closest races.

title: ASG recorded its dissatisfaction with budget cuts
body: Resolution 81-1, dated 21 April 1981, expressed ASG's dissatisfaction with budget cuts. It was filed with Resolution 81-2 on traffic tickets in the last days of the session, and it opens the numbering of a session that spent much of the following autumn on the state's cuts to higher education.

title: ASG petitioned the governor over cuts to higher education
body: In the spring ASG circulated a petition asking state government to weigh the importance of higher education in Kentucky's future before making further cuts, and sent it to Governor John Y. Brown, finance secretary George Atkins and the Council on Higher Education. The petition argued that a quality education required financial support for faculty and facilities. President Steve Fuller said many students did not realise how serious the cuts were, and that they meant dismissing faculty. The Talisman dates the petition only to the spring.

title: Bush opened his term saying students should understand ASG
body: Ellen Banahan's interview with the new president, Marcel Bush, ran in the second issue of the autumn under the line that he wanted students to understand the Associated Student Government. The same issue reported that campus police were offering a night escort service, a year before ASG and Interhall Council started a volunteer one of their own.

title: ASG submitted its budget
body: Ellen Banahan reported that ASG had submitted its budget for the year. It ran in the same issue as her first report that the organisation could not find the student discount cards it had ordered, and in a week the Herald headlined as the beginning of budget pleas across the university.

title: ASG executives defended their actions, and a former president was honoured
body: Ellen Banahan reported that the ASG executives had defended their actions, in the same issue that reported the campaign spending limit might be raised and that Steve Thornton, the 1978 ASG president, had been honoured. The defence came five days before the Herald's editorial page complained that petty politics plagued the organisation.

title: ASG asked for a book drop away from the library
body: Resolution 81-4, dated 22 September 1981, requested a book drop in a central location away from the library, reviving a request ASG had first made in November 1979 for a drop in the Downing University Center. Resolution 81-3, on parking spaces, carries the same date.

title: ASG considered barring freshmen from bringing cars to campus
body: Ellen Banahan reported that ASG was considering a plan to bar freshmen cars from campus. Parking ran through the session's legislation as well: Resolution 81-3 of 22 September dealt with parking spaces and Resolution 81-5 of 13 October with parking privileges.

title: ASG backed the budget protest as a petition reached the state council
body: Ellen Banahan reported that ASG supported the budget protest, in the same issue in which Wilma Norton reported a petition presented to the Council on Higher Education. Marcel Bush named the autumn's higher education rally as an achievement of his term when he resigned in January.

title: Bush appointed an ASG adviser
body: Tommy Newton reported that the ASG president had appointed an adviser. The question did not close with the appointment: after Bush resigned, his successor David Payne told the Herald in February that ASG wanted a second one.

title: A resolution on students' right to privacy
body: Resolution 81-6, dated 24 November 1981, concerned students' right to privacy, a year after the congress's long fight over dormitory room inspections and open house visitor lists. Resolution 81-9, on safety strips, carries the same date.

title: The discount cards left few happy
body: Kevin Francke's report on the student discount card scheme ran under the line that it had left few happy, and the same issue carried a second Francke piece reporting that many businesses were unhappy too. It closed a saga that had run since September: ASG could not find the cards, then found the printer's Texas telephone disconnected and its letter returned, then received 14,000 cards it did not hand out for weeks.

title: David Payne's appeal failed and a regent election was called
body: Kevin Francke reported that David Payne's appeal had failed and that an election for the student regent seat had been set. Payne had succeeded to the ASG presidency after Marcel Bush's resignation, and the Board of Regents minutes of 30 January 1982 name him as president. Under the previous arrangement the ASG president also sat as student regent, as Steve Fuller had. The seat instead went to a campus-wide vote and Sandra Norfleet won the runoff in February. The Herald index records the appeal and its failure but not the grounds on which it was made.

title: ASG heard two resolutions on state money and international students
body: The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government had heard two resolutions. Both are in SGA's own archive under the date 2 March 1982: Resolution 81-10 on the disbursement of state funds, and Resolution 81-11 asking that housing be provided for international students during the breaks when the dormitories close.

title: ASG asked for a grace week before finals
body: Resolution 81-12, dated 23 March 1982, requested a grace week between the last week of classes and finals week. It is the earliest of the calendar demands ASG returned to through the decade, which by 1985 included a fall mid-semester break and a week-long Thanksgiving.

title: The Herald argued a smaller ASG would be more effective
body: The Herald's editorial page argued that a smaller Associated Student Government would increase its effectiveness. It ran in the issue reporting Margaret Ragan's win in the repeated general election, and beside a letter applauding the University Center Board.

title: Marsupial Awards for ASG and the Herald, and a letter calling ASG a joke
body: Robert Carter's Marsupial Awards column handed prizes to both the Associated Student Government and the Herald, in the same issue that printed a letter from M. A. Baker headed that ASG was a joke. Baker had been the subject of a Herald feature in February 1981 describing him as fighting the system inside ASG. The pair closed a session that began with the paper complaining of petty politics and ended with the presidential election being run twice.

title: The student discount card came back with 17 merchants
body: The Herald's back-to-school issue reported that the student discount card carried 17 merchants. It succeeded the previous year's troubled card, which reached campus late, went undistributed for weeks and left students and businesses complaining by January. The card collapsed again the following autumn, when local merchants were left waiting for refunds.

src.label: College Heights Herald 58:1 Section A, 24 August 1982

title: ASG asked for transport for injured and disabled students
body: Resolution 82-1-F, dated 21 September 1982, requested special transportation from the Department of Public Safety for injured and handicapped students. It is the first numbered resolution of Margaret Ragan's session and the earliest transport proposal of a year that went on to put a campus shuttle service to a student vote.

src.label: SGA Resolution 82-1-F, Transportation for Injured or Handicapped

title: Jack Smith wrote in to applaud the escort service
body: Jack Smith wrote to the Herald applauding the student escort service, about eight weeks after the volunteer scheme run with Interhall Council and the university police began. The same issue reported that a concert by Alabama had packed Diddle Arena and that a small parade had ended the Homecoming weekend.

title: ASG supported the football proposal before the regents
body: Jamie Morton reported that ASG supported the football proposal the Board of Regents was to consider at its Saturday session, alongside the bookstore. The same issue reported ticket sales down $20,000 as 1982 attendance declined, carried a Herald editorial urging the regents to veto more football spending, and printed a letter calling concert apathy pathetic.

title: ASG proposed that athletic fees replace student game tickets
body: Resolution 82-8-S, dated 8 February 1983, proposed that students use their athletic fees to get into games rather than individual tickets being sold. It followed the previous session's Resolution 81-8, which had asked only that the ticket price be cut, and preceded the outgoing congress's endorsement of a $15 athletic fee in April.

src.label: SGA Resolution 82-8-S, Termination of Student Ticket Sales

title: ASG backed free admission to games
body: Jamie Morton reported that ASG supported the plan for free admission to athletic events, and a companion piece in the same issue reported that support for free game admission was growing. It was the public face of Resolution 82-8-S, filed nine days earlier.

title: ASG asked for a review of textbook policy at the bookstore
body: Resolution 82-9-S, dated 22 March 1983, requested a review of the College Heights Bookstore's new and used textbook policies. ASG had pressed the bookstore before, asking in January 1980 that it adopt a break-even policy on books, and the regents took the bookstore up themselves in January 1983.

title: Few women were using the escort service
body: Gary Elmore reported that few women were using the student escort service, in the same issue in which Jamie Morton reported ASG discussing its plans for the following year. The same issue reported the University Center Board satisfied with its concert series.

title: Local merchants waited for refunds on the discount cards
body: Steve Paul reported that local merchants were waiting for refunds over the student discount cards. The card had been ASG's flagship service project of the autumn and had drawn a Herald editorial in September saying the organisation should govern rather than market cards. By November ASG had given up on the outside company and printed the cards itself.

title: An A-minus was floated for the grade plan
body: Steve Paul reported that an A-minus might be added to the Associated Student Government's grade plan, and the Herald's editorial page argued in the same issue that a new grade scale must include one. The plan had been approved five days earlier, and by 8 December a group had organised against it.

title: A group opposed the grade plan, and false proposals were said to risk impeachment
body: Steve Paul reported that a group had come out against ASG's grade plan, five weeks after the congress approved it. The same issue carried a second Paul piece reporting that writing false proposals could mean impeachment, in a semester in which the Herald had already reported ASG voiding its own procedures.

title: ASG urged to take up student rights
body: Barry Rose reported that ASG had been encouraged to look at student rights, and the Herald's editorial page argued in the same issue that the student rights policy needed re-examining. A week later Mark Edelen reported that ASG would examine rights. The issue also reported that a day-care centre was possible in the autumn, a project ASG had taken up in November.

title: ASG announced a poll on beer at athletic events
body: Mark Edelen reported that ASG would poll students on whether they wanted beer sold at games. This is the announcement of the poll, not its result. By 16 February the paper was reporting that an NCAA rule might prevent alcohol sales at ballgames and by 23 February that the NCAA and the Sun Belt would allow them. The poll itself went ahead on general election day in April, by then framed around beer and a campus pub, and low turnout threatened a revote.

title: ASG wanted evaluation changes but opposed achievement tests
body: Mark Edelen reported that the Associated Student Government wanted changes to faculty evaluation while opposing achievement tests. The same issue carried a Herald editorial arguing that linking the Kentucky Intercollegiate State Legislature to ASG would be a mistake, and a letter from Vincent Lewis praising ASG. The legislature delayed its move the following week.

title: ASG, the centre board and Interhall Council found their duties overlapped
body: Mark Edelen reported that the Associated Student Government, the University Center Board and the Interhall Council overlapped in what they did. The ground had been divided between them five years earlier, when the regents moved campus entertainment and the money that paid for it from ASG to the centre board.

title: The Herald said dropping the campus pub was a good move
body: The Herald's editorial page said the Associated Student Government had made a good move by dropping the pub issue. It closed the alcohol question that had run through the previous spring's student poll, and the congress opened it again in November 1985.

title: ASG proposed a new required class
body: Chad Carlton reported that the Associated Student Government had proposed a new required class. It came in the same week the congress could point to four proposals already carried out, and eight days before its grade scale proposal was denied.

title: ASG asked for lot signs and safety railings
body: Victoria Malmer reported that the Associated Student Government had proposed parking lot signs and safety railings. The request followed a fall in the parking structure a week earlier, which the Herald had reported alongside safety director Paul Bunch's comment that the accident was unpreventable.

title: ASG moved to end the class attendance policy
body: Victoria Malmer reported that ASG wanted to end the university's class attendance policy, and the Herald's editorial page argued the same day that dealing with attendance ills could make things fairer. Kevin Knapp drew an editorial cartoon on excused absences in the same issue.

title: Vice President George Bush was announced to visit campus
body: The Herald of 25 October 1984 reported that Vice President George Bush would visit Western the following day, and its editorial page urged faculty to cancel classes for the visit. The digitised index carries the notice but no report of the visit itself, so nothing is recorded here about what happened on the day.

title: Few voted in the autumn ASG election
body: Victoria Malmer reported that few students had voted in the Associated Student Government election. A week later LaMont Jones dropped out of the revote and Kevin Knapp drew a cartoon on the organisation. Turnout was the theme of the whole year: by February the Herald was reporting that election apathy was hurting ASG.

title: Student government announced it would organise the book exchange
body: Victoria Malmer reported that student government was planning to organise the book exchange, and a companion item in the same issue described a programme to give students a choice of textbooks. By the end of November the Herald was reporting that ASG was promoting the exchange, and the first printed exchange list appeared at the start of the spring semester.

title: Two resolutions passed as the book exchange won its first praise
body: The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government had approved two resolutions, and printed a letter from Scott Vick applauding an ASG plan. Stan Reagan's column in the same issue argued that the book exchange would make money later but greater.

title: Apathy in the elections, and a summer for the book exchange
body: Mack Humphreys reported that election apathy was hurting the Associated Student Government. The same issue carried a short item that the book exchange was planned for the summer, a week after the paper had reported the venture might take a summer vacation instead.

title: ASG proposed cancelling classes for snow as needed
body: Bill 85-3-F, dated 8 October 1985, proposed that classes be cancelled because of snow as needed rather than on a fixed schedule. It is one of a run of small practical bills in Mitchell McKinney's term, filed a week after the bill creating the Financial Advisory Council.

title: ASG reconsidered child care as the Herald told it to represent students
body: Kim Parson reported that ASG was reconsidering child care, a question the congress had first taken up in November 1983. The same issue carried a Herald opinion piece saying ASG needed to start representing students and a Kevin Knapp editorial cartoon on the organisation, and reported that the field of candidates for the university presidency had been narrowed to about 20.

title: ASG pushed to merge the student ID and the SuperCard
body: Resolution 85-14-F, dated 3 December 1985, proposed creating a single card combining the student ID and the SuperCard. It followed Bill 85-12-F of 19 November, which asked that use of the SuperCard be extended across campus. The same night's Bill 85-15-F asked that ASG produce its own student discount card, after the outside printer's failures that autumn.

src.label: SGA Resolution 85-14-F, Student ID Card and SuperCard Merger

title: ASG joined the higher education rally in Frankfort
body: ASG joined students, faculty and administrators from Western at the state-wide rally for higher education held at the Frankfort Civic Center on 6 February 1986 and sponsored by Kentucky Advocates for Higher Education. Chartered buses left from in front of Downing University Center for the three-hour journey, carrying Spirit Masters, cheerleaders, pep bands, reporters, teachers and administrators, and the administration wrote to teachers asking them to excuse students who went. Every university in the state was represented, and Governor Martha Layne Collins and former North Carolina governor James Hunt spoke.

title: Greg Elder filed for the top job as the deadline neared
body: Jackie Hutcherson reported that the filing deadline was Friday and that administrative vice president Greg Elder had filed for the ASG presidency, two days after Mitchell McKinney withdrew from the race. The same issue carried a Herald opinion piece by Steve Reagan arguing that ASG had to develop goals and priorities, and letters from Meredith Gainer and Loree Zimmerman defending the organisation.

title: Few watched four candidates debate, and the Herald endorsed nobody
body: Jackie Hutcherson reported that few people watched the four candidates for the ASG presidency debate. The paper printed profiles of Greg Elder, Andy Hollifield, Terry Malone and Tim Todd and then declined to back any of them, running an editorial headed that no candidate stood out and endorsing a fictional Joe Ideal instead. The same issue reported ASG proposing that faculty return tests to students, the subject of Bill 86-15-S filed nine days earlier.

title: ASG asked for a campus map at Downing University Center
body: Bill 86-34-S, dated 8 April 1986, requested that a campus map be placed at the Downing University Center. It was one of ten bills the outgoing congress filed that night, among them Bill 86-35-S asking for a scholarship for students from Santo Domingo de los Colorados, Bowling Green's sister city, and Bill 86-37-S for bulletin boards in the Downing University Center lift.

src.label: SGA Bill 86-34-S, Placing of a Campus Map

title: Elder named the session's three achievements
body: Administrative vice president Greg Elder told the Talisman that ASG counted three bills as its main accomplishments of the year: having the English 101 pass/fail moved, reducing the hours a student needed to live in Poland Hall, and producing the book exchange programme. ASG was one of five organisations whose presidents met once a month over breakfast, a group the yearbook called the Big Five, with Interhall Council, Spirit Masters, the Interfraternity Council and the Panhellenic Council.

title: McKinney sat on the search that chose Kern Alexander
body: As student regent, ASG president Mitchell McKinney took an active part in Western's search for a president, which produced Kern Alexander after the board screened applicants, visited candidates on their own campuses and interviewed the finalists. McKinney also sat as a voting member of the University Center Board and the Education Advisory Committee, led a congress of about 100 members, and told the Talisman he intended to go on to graduate school and teach at university level.

title: International Day held three weeks of the congress's attention
body: International Day was ASG business through the autumn of 1986. The minutes of 14 October record it alongside events and discount cards, those of 21 October record it alongside elections and legislation, and those of 28 October record it with the Legislative Research Committee and the Student Action Committee. The minutes do not record how the day itself went.

title: Alphabet Day recurs across the year's minutes
body: Alphabet Day appears three times in the surviving 1986-87 minutes: on 23 September 1986 with elections, the retreat and committee appointments, on 24 February 1987 with the faculty reception and the high school leadership conference, and on 17 March 1987 with the spring conference and the lecture series. The minutes name it without describing it.

title: A joint hot dog supper with the University Center Board
body: On 3 October 1986 Tim Harper and David Rodriguez sent a joint invitation to the members of student government and of the University Center Board to a hot dog supper. The invitation survives in SGA's own records; the archive's description names the two men but gives them no offices.

src.label: SGA correspondence, Hot Dog Supper, 3 October 1986

title: A lecture series and a Young Democrats versus Young Republicans debate
body: The minutes of 25 November 1986 record a lecture series and a debate between the Young Democrats and the Young Republicans among the congress's business, together with legislation and a Kentucky student government association meeting at Western. The lecture series returns in the minutes of 17 March 1987, and debates again in those of 24 March 1987. What was scheduled is recorded; no account of either event survives in the minutes.

title: Lieutenant Governor Steve Beshear's visit comes before the congress
body: The minutes of 31 March 1987 record a visit by Lieutenant Governor Steve Beshear alongside the state student government meeting, other events and resolutions. This is a note of what was arranged; the minutes do not report the visit itself.

title: A faculty reception breakfast and the book exchange
body: The minutes of 17 February 1987 record a faculty reception breakfast and the book exchange among the congress's business, with legislation and the committee meeting schedule. The faculty reception returns in the minutes of 24 February 1987 alongside a high school leadership conference.

title: Todd went to Wisconsin to look at a campus hangout
body: The minutes of 18 November 1986 record ASG president Tim Todd's trip to Wisconsin about a campus hangout, alongside the Western-Notre Dame game and legislation. The hangout in Downing University Center was one of the two projects the 1987 Talisman named as ASG's main work that year, and the minutes of 24 March 1987 return to it.

title: ASG asked for the mandatory athletic fee to be abolished
body: Resolution 86-8-F, dated 14 October 1986, proposed ending the student athletic fee. The same meeting took Resolution 86-9-F, asking Campus Police to issue a warning rather than a ticket for a first offence.

src.label: Resolution 86-8-F, Abolishment of Mandatory Athletic Fee, 14 October 1986

title: Two academic resolutions on one night: the W and a reading day
body: On 18 November 1986 the congress took Resolution 86-14-F, asking that the W for a withdrawn course be removed from student transcripts, and Resolution 86-15-F, asking for a reading day before final exams. The study day request was still being made by successive congresses into the 1990s.

title: One member wrote most of the congress's bills
body: The Herald of 11 December 1986 reported that a single member of Associated Student Government, Bill Schilling, wrote most of the bills that came before the congress. Schilling was the author of the recorded campus events phone line proposal tabled that February, and he was at the centre of the impeachment attempt the following autumn.

title: The Herald's verdict on the year: conflicts and walkouts
body: Leigh Eagleston's piece in the Herald of 23 April 1987 summed up the ASG year under the headline that conflicts and walkouts had finished it off. It ran in the last issues of the spring term, after the amendment that died for want of members and the disputed presidential race.

title: Kern Alexander installed as Western's president
body: The minutes of 11 November 1986 record the installation of Kern Alexander as Western's president among the congress's business, with fall enrolment, the spring conference and the Western-Notre Dame game. Alexander had been named president that August; he resigned in the spring of 1988.

title: Bill Schilling lost his ASG seat when the hall association refused him leave
body: The Herald of 27 October 1987 reported that Bill Schilling was out after the Residence Hall Association denied him a leave of absence. The Herald had named Schilling the year before as the member who wrote most of the congress's bills. The same issue carried ASG's move to get tough on absenteeism. The report does not say which seat he lost, and the congress began an impeachment process against him three weeks later.

title: The congress began an impeachment process against Bill Schilling
body: Jill Duff reported in the Herald of 19 November 1987 that student government had begun an impeachment process against Bill Schilling. The proceeding did not go the distance: two issues later the Herald reported that the request for impeachment had been dropped.

title: The impeachment request was dropped
body: The Herald of 3 December 1987 reported that student government had dropped its request for impeachment. The following week's issue reported that Schilling was instead placed under the eye of a watchdog committee, carried a piece in which William Fogle explained the congress's actions, and ran three letters on it, including one defending the rescission and one from Van C. Hodge Jr. saying the issue was not closed.

title: A watchdog committee, and a page of letters about it
body: The Herald of 10 December 1987 reported that Bill Schilling was under the eye of a watchdog committee, and printed William Fogle's explanation of student government's actions beside letters from Hollie Hale defending the rescission, Kevin Hargrave calling an editorial an attack, and Van C. Hodge Jr. writing that the student government issue remained.

title: The Herald blamed diversity of opinion for the congress's conflicts
body: Dorren Klausnitzer's article in the Herald of 28 January 1988 attributed student government's conflicts to diversity. The same issue ran an editorial calling that a poor excuse. It appeared seven weeks after the Schilling watchdog committee and five weeks before the Herald reported that ASG's chief officers rarely kept their office hours.

title: Bill Schilling ran for president months after the impeachment attempt
body: The minutes of 1 March 1988 record Bill Schilling running for the presidency of student government, four months after the Herald reported him out following the Residence Hall Association's refusal of a leave of absence, and three months after the congress dropped its impeachment request. He was not among the two candidates the Herald reported surviving the primaries on 31 March.

title: A tuition rally and a flyer on the proposed budget freeze
body: The minutes of 1 March 1988 record a tuition rally, and the file preserves with them a flyer on the state budget and a proposed budget freeze for Western. It followed the Frankfort higher education rally that ASG had backed a fortnight earlier.

title: The six awards the congress gave at its banquet
body: A description of awards filed with the minutes of 15 March 1988 lists the six honours the congress presented: the Dero Downing Award, Outstanding Congress Member, Outstanding Committee Member, the Dean Charles A. Keown Award, the Kerrie Faye Stewart Memorial Award and the Mary Angela Norcia Award. The Norcia award had been created only the month before, in memory of a member who had died the previous summer.

src.label: ASG meeting minutes and description of awards, 15 March 1988

title: A campus ticket sales outlet proposed
body: Resolution 88-9-S, dated 12 April 1988, proposed a ticket sales outlet on campus and set out in detail what it called a Centritic Sales Office. It was one of the last pieces of business of Tim Todd's second term.

title: Weekend hours asked for Unicorn Pizza and the campus theatre
body: Resolution 88-10-S, dated 19 April 1988, asked that Unicorn Pizza be open at weekends. The same request came back through successive congresses: Resolution 89-2-F in October 1989 asked for the weekend hours to be expanded, and the administration granted them on a trial basis.

src.label: Resolution 88-10-S, Unicorn Pizza and Theater Open on Weekends, 19 April 1988

title: The Herald found the chief officers rarely kept office hours
body: Dorren Klausnitzer reported in the Herald of 3 March 1988 that Associated Student Government's chief officers rarely kept their office hours, and the same issue editorialised that published hours mean little if they are not kept. It ran nine days after the organisation had publicly explained its empty seats, and in the same season as the editorial telling it to find better ideas than gimmicks.

title: The Herald reported that Cambron had made false claims
body: Dorren Klausnitzer reported in the Herald of 26 April 1988 that Bruce Cambron, who a fortnight earlier had called for a new presidential election over the write-in votes, had made some false claims. Cambron took the complaint on regardless, raising it with university president Thomas Meredith the following October.

title: Vote America ran through the first month of the term
body: Vote America is in the minutes of 13, 20 and 27 September 1988, in a presidential election autumn. The 20 September meeting set it beside a lecture series, International Day, College Awareness Day and the Student Alumni Association; the 27 September meeting set it beside committee service and Panhellenic activities. The drive ran before the mock presidential election ASG staged with the College Republicans in October.

title: A lecture series, College Awareness Day and the Student Alumni Association
body: The minutes of 20 September 1988 record a lecture series, College Awareness Day and the Student Alumni Association among the congress's business, together with a meeting with the Council for Higher Education, a visit from the University of Louisville student government, International Day and constitutional amendments. The minutes name what was planned rather than what happened.

title: International Day again, with homecoming
body: International Day ran through the autumn of 1988 as it had in 1986: the minutes of 20 September, 11 October and 18 October all record it. The 11 October meeting took it alongside homecoming, the student alumni association and the member of the week awards.

title: Big Red's Roar and the bus stop shelters
body: The minutes of 25 October 1988 record Big Red's Roar, the mock election and bus stop shelters. Big Red's Roar returns in the minutes of 7 February 1989. The minutes place ASG in the event without saying what its part was.

title: A Christmas dance, a faculty reception and sponsored basketball games
body: The minutes of 28 November 1988 record a Christmas dance, a faculty reception and the sponsoring of basketball games, alongside the teacher evaluations work. The following week's minutes add a Christmas reception.

title: Martin Luther King Jr Day recognised at Western
body: The minutes of 6 December 1988 record that the Martin Luther King Jr holiday was now recognised at Western. Student government had put a Martin Luther King bill through a divided congress in March 1987, a year after it had rejected dismissing classes for the holiday. The same meeting covered the Council for Higher Education, electronic mail, newsletters, a Christmas reception and the book exchange.

title: Campus Pride is Western Wide
body: The minutes of 17 January 1989 record a programme called Campus Pride is Western Wide, alongside the use of the hotline ASG had set up the previous October and a review of the autumn's legislation. The following week's minutes carry it as Campus Pride '89.

title: ASG Awareness Week
body: The minutes of 31 January and 7 February 1989 both record an ASG Awareness Week, set beside bus shelter construction, public relations, the General Education proposal and the State Student Government Conference. The organisation ran a comparable week under the name Anti-Apathy Week the following year.

title: An Oozeball tournament
body: The minutes of 28 February and 14 March 1989 both record an Oozeball tournament, the mud volleyball event. The Herald of 4 April 1989 carried a piece on Oozeball by Dresden Wall, in the same issue as a report that the presidential field would be shaved by two that day.

title: Two weekends built to keep students on campus
body: The minutes of 21 March 1989 record a Hell No, We Won't Go weekend, and those of 28 March 1989 a Stay and Play Weekend, alongside the ASG banquet and the shuttle shelter construction. Keeping students on campus at weekends had been the stated aim of the Downing University Center hangout project two years earlier.

title: A Senior Send-Off closed the year
body: The last surviving minutes of the spring, dated 4 April 1989, record a Senior Send-Off alongside open positions and the book exchange. It came a week after the minutes recording the ASG banquet and the installation of Thomas Meredith.

title: The secretary resigned in January
body: The minutes of 24 January 1989 record the resignation of Mickie Hennig as secretary, alongside shuttle stops and Campus Pride '89. The minutes record the resignation without giving a reason.

title: Bids taken for the shuttle shelters ASG had asked for
body: Having asked in Resolutions 88-2-F and 88-3-F of 1 November 1988 for shelters and benches at the Big Red shuttle stops, the congress followed the job through the spring. The minutes of 31 January 1989 record shelter construction, those of 7 February record shelter bids, and those of 21 February, 21 March and 28 March all return to the shelters.

title: A student athletic promotions committee proposed
body: Resolution 89-2-S, dated 14 February 1989, proposed creating a student athletic promotions committee to push attendance at athletic events up. The minutes of the following week, 21 February, record a basketball game among the congress's business.

src.label: Resolution 89-2-S, Student Athletic Promotions Committee, 14 February 1989

title: A Sunday matinee at the campus theatre
body: Resolution 89-4-S, dated 21 February 1989, asked for a Sunday matinee to be added at the campus theatre. Two more resolutions carried the same date, 89-5-S asking that the library stay open until 10 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays, and 89-6-S asking that men's intramural basketball and volleyball be played at weekends. The push for more film hours reached the Herald a week later.

title: More coed dorms and a later spring break
body: The Herald of 23 March 1989 reported that Associated Student Government wanted more coed dormitories and a later spring break. The two requests are in the legislation as Resolution 89-7-S of 20 March, moving spring break to the third week of March, and Resolution 89-8-S of 21 March, converting a residence hall without air conditioning to coed housing.

title: Thomas Meredith installed as Western's president
body: The minutes of 28 March 1989 record the installation of Thomas Meredith as Western's president among the congress's business, alongside the shuttle shelter construction, the ASG banquet and the Stay and Play Weekend. Meredith addressed an ASG meeting in January, and returned repeatedly over the following five years.

title: A student government organised itself on the Glasgow campus
body: On 21 September 1989 the students of Western's Glasgow campus held an organisational meeting to settle a name, officers and elections for a student body of their own. A week later, on 28 September, the first executive council of the WKU-Glasgow Associated Student Government met, took homecoming and Christmas activities, drew up by-laws, and made a list of businesses to approach about homecoming. The Bowling Green congress had voted in August to include Glasgow representatives, and its minutes of 19 September record a Glasgow campus constitution.

src.label: Associated Student Body-Glasgow organisational meeting minutes, 21 September 1989

title: Glasgow's homecoming, Red and White Day and Women in Transition
body: The Glasgow student government's minutes of 6 October 1989 record homecoming events, elections, a Red and White Day, Women in Transition and Christmas activities. Its minutes of 13 October return to homecoming and fundraising, and those of 27 October add daycare and a book exchange. This is the founding programme of a student government that had existed for a fortnight.

src.label: Associated Student Body-Glasgow meeting minutes, 6 October 1989

title: Glasgow planned Christmas activities and a parade
body: The Glasgow student government's minutes of 10 November 1989 record Christmas activities, fundraising and a parade. Its minutes of 4 November and its report of 1 December are given over to the same preparations, the last surviving Glasgow record of the year.

src.label: Associated Student Body-Glasgow meeting minutes, 10 November 1989

title: Big Red Day for the mascot's tenth birthday
body: Resolution 89-9-F, dated 28 November 1989, made 2 December 1989 Big Red Day in honour of the mascot's tenth anniversary. The minutes of 14 November record Big Red's tenth birthday alongside the counselling centre and a leadership reception, and those of 28 November return to it with the tuition increase.

title: A Mitch McConnell lecture put on the congress's agenda
body: The minutes of 13 March 1990 record a Mitch McConnell lecture alongside a Drug Awareness and Health Enrichment Week and the coming elections. McConnell was then Kentucky's junior United States senator. The minutes record what was arranged; they do not report the lecture.

title: Gatewood Galbraith spoke on legalising drugs
body: The Herald of 22 March 1990 reported Gatewood Galbraith arguing for the legalisation of drugs, in a piece by Angie Jones. The minutes of 20 March 1990 record a Gatewood Galbraith lecture on the legalisation of drugs alongside elections and open positions.

title: Earth Day, Earth Week and a tree planting
body: Earth Day is in the minutes of 20 February 1990 with the telephone surveys and the elections, Earth Week in those of 27 February and 10 April, and a tree planting in those of 3 April. The 1990 Earth Day was its twentieth anniversary and the Herald reported on 24 April that its organisers hoped public interest would hold.

title: A reception for the regent, and Challenge of Change
body: The minutes of 16 January 1990 record a reception for the regent, a Challenge of Change programme, a Student Council Day and a student rights meeting. The regent's reception is in the minutes of 23 and 30 January as well, and Challenge of Change in those of 23 January.

title: A Valentine's dance and the organisational presidents roundtable
body: The minutes of 13 February 1990 record a Valentine's dance and the organisational presidents roundtable, with parking, awards and vacancies. The roundtable was put on a formal footing that autumn by Bill 90-2-F.

title: Alcohol Awareness Week
body: The minutes of 3 October 1989 record an Alcohol Awareness Week alongside the master plan committee, training sessions, the shuttle shelter, condoms and International Day. Alcohol came back before the congress on 7 November, when the minutes record petitions on alcohol and on twenty-four hour visitation.

title: Kentucky Higher Education Week and a professor of the year
body: The minutes of 10 October 1989 record Kentucky Higher Education Week, homecoming, and Luther Hughes as professor of the year. A leadership reception follows in the minutes of 14 November.

title: Unicorn Pizza's weekend hours were granted on trial
body: Correspondence dated 27 October 1989 replied to Resolution 89-2-F by expanding Unicorn Pizza's weekend hours on a trial basis. The congress had asked for the extension on 10 October, after the Herald reported the demand on 12 October and then drew ASG and the administration riding a unicorn. It is one of the year's few requests with a recorded answer.

src.label: SGA correspondence on Unicorn Pizza, 27 October 1989

title: A recorded information line asked for again
body: Resolution 90-2-S, dated 16 January 1990, asked for a recorded announcement telephone line. The congress had tabled the same idea in February 1987, when the equipment was costed at $500 with $60 for installation and $17 a month, and had set up a Wednesday afternoon hotline instead in October 1988.

title: A freshman orientation programme asked for
body: Resolution 90-1-S, dated 16 January 1990, asked for a freshman orientation programme. Correspondence answering it survives in the SGA records dated 24 January 1990.

title: New Rock 92 asked for on the university centre speakers
body: Resolution 90-8-S asked that WWHR, the student station then branded New Rock 92, be played over the Downing University Center speakers. The archive dates the resolution 6 January 1990.

title: ASG endorsed the fee rise that built the Preston Center
body: Resolution 90-18-S, dated 17 April 1990, approved the Board of Regents' increase in the student fee used to pay construction costs for the Preston Health and Activities Center. The regents set the 1990-91 budget and tuition six weeks later.
money: student construction fee increase approved by the regents

src.label: Resolution 90-18-S, Preston Health & Activities Center Construction Fees, 17 April 1990

title: A resolution on getting into the buildings
body: Resolution 90-17-S, dated 10 April 1990, asked for improvements to the accessibility of campus buildings. It was one of the last pieces of legislation of Amos Gott's term.

title: Two twenty-four hour visitation halls asked for
body: Resolution 90-13-S, dated 20 March 1990, asked for two residence halls with twenty-four hour coed visitation. The minutes of 24 October 1989 record twenty-four hour visitation among the congress's business, and those of 7 November record petitions on it and on alcohol.

title: A student food services committee, and a forum with it
body: Resolution 89-6-F, dated 31 October 1989, asked for a student advisory food services committee. The minutes of 24 October record a food service forum, and correspondence answering the resolution survives dated 9 November 1989. The same 31 October meeting produced Resolution 89-4-F on weekend library hours.

title: The year opened with Glasgow seats and a Judicial Board
body: The first minutes of the term, dated 29 August 1989, record Judicial Board candidates, an explanation of procedures, the inclusion of Glasgow representatives, committee organisational reports and the freshman elections. Three bylaw amendments followed on 5 September, on the president's board, on how legislation was to be written and submitted, and on the order of business.

title: SGA started a newsletter called The Gavel
body: Student government published a newsletter, The Gavel, whose first issue the archive dates October 1993. It ran beside the Word on Western radio show the congress named that same month. The archive holds a second issue filed under April 1994, though its catalogue description reads volume one, issue two, April 1992.

title: Bill 94-4-F asked every member to talk to 25 students a week
body: Bill 94-4-F, dated 4 October 1994, proposed that each SGA representative speak with twenty-five students each week about the association's work. It is one of a run of internal-outreach measures from the Evans administration held in SGA's own records on TopSCHOLAR.

title: Two bills bought flags for Diddle Arena and the Kentucky Library
body: On 1 November 1994 the congress took up two companion bills: Bill 94-7-F requested the purchase of WKU flags for Diddle Arena and the Kentucky Library and Museum, and Bill 94-6-F requested Kentucky state flags for the same two buildings. Flags recur in SGA's records through the decade, reappearing in the 1995-96 and 1996-97 minutes.

title: SGA backed free housing for resident assistants
body: Resolution 94-9-F, dated 1 November 1994, asked the university for an increased housing subsidy for resident assistants. The Herald reported the position the following week under Mitchell Quarles's byline.

src.label: Herald 70:22, 10 Nov 1994 - Quarles, "Student Government Association Endorses Free Resident Assistant Housing"

title: Two resolutions backed the band council's transport problems
body: On 8 November 1994 the congress passed a pair of resolutions for the WKU Band Council. Resolution 94-17-F asked for a shuttle service from Diddle Arena to Van Meter for public concerts, and Resolution 94-16-F supported a van to move band instruments across campus for football games.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Resolution 94-17-F, Support for WKU Band Council Public Concert Shuttle Service

title: A non-circulating textbook library proposed
body: Resolution 94-18-F, dated 15 November 1994, asked the university to create a non-circulating textbook library so students could consult required texts without buying them. It sat alongside the book exchange the same administration had run in October.

title: Resolution 94-20-F sought to stop undergraduates grading papers
body: Resolution 94-20-F, dated 22 November 1994, asked that undergraduate teaching assistants be disallowed from grading papers and proctoring tests. It closed a fall session in which the congress also asked for faculty evaluations in both semesters, under Resolution 94-14-F of 8 November.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Resolution 94-20-F, Discontinuing Undergraduate Student Teaching Assistants Participation in Grading Process

title: A painted crosswalk and six trash cans
body: Two resolutions dated 31 January 1995 dealt with the ground between the parking structure and Smith Stadium. Resolution 95-3-S proposed a painted crosswalk to the parking garage and Resolution 95-4-S requested six trash cans along Big Red Way.

title: A roommate selection guide for freshmen
body: Resolution 95-7-S, dated 11 April 1995, proposed creating a freshman roommate selection guide. It was among the last measures of Rob Evans's year, passed in the same week as the Sibling's Day resolution.

title: Tara Higdon's first meeting: a state conference and committee setup
body: The congress met on 29 August 1995 from 5.05 to 5.40 p.m. SGA's own record of the meeting describes business on the State Student Government Conference, elections and setting up committees, the first meeting of Tara Higdon's term held in the digitised minutes.

title: A voter registration drive, a pep rally and organizational aid
body: The meeting of 9 September 1995 took up a voter registration drive, a pep rally and organizational aid. It is the earliest record in this year of the three strands that made up most of SGA's public programme work: registering students to vote, backing athletics events and paying out money to campus clubs.

title: Bill 95-1-F tied organizational aid to showing up
body: Bill 95-1-F, dated 19 September 1995, required any organization receiving SGA aid to have a representative participating in SGA. It made attendance a condition of the money at a time when the Herald was reporting falling interest in the association.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 95-1-F, Organizational Aid Recipients on COA

title: Resolution 95-1-F asked for the running track to be replaced
body: Resolution 95-1-F, dated 19 September 1995, requested that the running track be replaced and widened. Track resurfacing had been an SGA request since Resolution 93-8-S, on resurfacing the Smith Stadium track, in 1993.

title: Weekend in the Woods
body: The meeting of 26 September 1995 discussed Weekend in the Woods, a code of conduct and open positions on the congress. The archive's record names the event but not its programme, so nothing is known here beyond that SGA had it in hand that autumn.

title: Homecoming, and members sent out to speak to classes
body: On 2 October 1995 the congress discussed homecoming, a plan for SGA members to speak to classes, and its open positions. Speaking to classes was the association's standing answer to the visibility problem the Herald returned to all year.

title: Midnight Mania, phone registration and a parliamentary workshop
body: The meeting of 10 October 1995 took up registration by telephone, a parliamentary procedure workshop for members, and Midnight Mania, the midnight start of basketball practice. The workshop ran again the following week.

title: Coach for a Game, a student leader reception and Topline
body: On 17 October 1995 the congress discussed Topline telephone registration, the parliamentary procedure workshop, the Coach for a Game contest and a student leader reception. Coach for a Game had been created by Bill 92-03-S in 1992 and was still running four years later.

title: Paving Creason lot, and a handrail
body: Two resolutions carry the date 17 October 1995. Resolution 95-3-F asked that the Creason parking lot be paved and Resolution 95-4-F requested a handrail by the Schneider Hall drive.

title: Faculty evaluations, a recycling plan and the New Level report
body: The meeting of 24 October 1995 discussed faculty evaluations, recommendations arising from the university's Moving to a New Level review, a recycling plan and a meeting with Dave Parrot. Faculty evaluations dominated the congress's autumn and ran into a missed deadline in November.

title: Discount cards, surveys and credit for hall assistants
body: On 31 October 1995 the congress discussed SGA surveys, discount cards and academic credit for residence hall assistants. A student discount card had been an SGA product since Bill 85-15-F a decade earlier.

title: Security cameras for the parking garage
body: Resolution 95-8-F, dated 7 November 1995, requested security cameras in the parking garage and the parking lots. It belongs to the run of campus-safety measures that began with the emergency phones of the previous spring and continued with the lighting resolution later that month.

title: Faculty evaluations, community service and door scanners
body: The meeting of 14 November 1995 ran from 5.00 to 5.50 p.m., the longest autumn meeting in the digitised minutes, and covered faculty evaluations, community service and door security scanners. Two days later the Herald reported that SGA would miss its deadline on the evaluations.

title: An academic service fee to cover add and drop costs
body: Resolution 95-9-F, dated 14 November 1995, asked for the creation of an academic service fee to cover the cost of adding and dropping classes. The Herald reported the following week that the congress would vote on the drop/add fee proposal.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Resolution 95-9-F, Establish an Academic Service Fee

title: SGA missed its deadline on faculty evaluations
body: The Herald of 16 November 1995 reported that the Student Government Association would miss its deadline for faculty evaluations, under Charbonee LaBelle's byline. Publishing evaluations had been SGA policy since Resolution 94-1-S and would still be an unfinished project when Amanda Coates revived it in 2000.

src.label: Herald 71:24, 16 Nov 1995 - LaBelle, "Student Government Association to Miss Deadline for Evaluations"

title: A vote on the drop/add fee
body: The Herald of 21 November 1995 reported that SGA would vote on a drop/add fee proposal. The proposal is Resolution 95-9-F of the previous week, which asked for an academic service fee to cover the cost of adding and dropping classes.

src.label: Herald 71:25, 21 Nov 1995 - LaBelle, "Student Government Association to Vote on Drop/Add Fee Proposal"

title: Big Red Dollar scanners and more lights
body: Two resolutions carry the date 21 November 1995. Resolution 95-10-F asked for scanners that accept Big Red Dollars in the library and at the Department of Public Safety, and Resolution 95-11-F requested lights in parking lots and walkways to make the campus safer.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Resolution 95-10-F, Big Red Scanners in Library & Public Safety Department

title: President for a Day and a time management forum
body: The last meeting of the autumn, on 28 November 1995, discussed the President for a Day contest, a time management forum and the congress's open positions. President for a Day had been established by Bill 91-9-F four years earlier.

title: The spring opened with two contests and a reception for legislators
body: The first meeting of 1996, on 16 January, discussed emergency phones, a reception for state legislators, President for a Day and Coach for a Day. The legislators' reception recurs in the minutes of 23 January, 27 February and 5 March.

title: Healthy Loving Week and a Valentine's Day game show
body: On 23 January 1996 the congress discussed December graduation, the legislators' reception, Healthy Loving Week and a Valentine's Day game show. Healthy Loving Week was still on the agenda at the meeting of 13 February.

title: Bowl for Kids' Sake and the Russellville distance learning site
body: The meeting of 30 January 1996 discussed changes in academic departments, the Russellville distance learning site and Bowl for Kids' Sake. The bowling fundraiser returned to SGA's agenda in November 1996 and again in January 1997.

title: One meeting held the whole of the spring's business
body: The record of the 13 February 1996 meeting lists the search for a vice president for academic affairs, Healthy Loving Week, the President for a Day contest, vacancies, the budget, a newsletter, Coming Home and the University Boulevard skywalk.

title: Certificates for the president's and dean's lists
body: Resolution 96-4-S, dated 20 February 1996, asked that certificates be given to students who make the president's and dean's lists. Recognising high-achieving students had been an SGA project since Bill 91-7-S on presidential scholars.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Resolution 96-4-S, Certificate for President's and Dean's List

title: Bill 96-2-S opened the constitution
body: Bill 96-2-S, dated 20 February 1996, requested changes in the SGA constitution. The amendments reached the ballot in April, when Herald letters urged students to approve them alongside the presidential vote.

title: Diddle Dollars, a phonathon and the flags again
body: The meeting of 5 March 1996 discussed Diddle Dollars, the legislative reception, WKU flags and a phonathon; the previous week's meeting of 27 February had covered Diddle Dollars, the legislator reception and open positions. These are the last two meetings of the year in the digitised minutes.

title: A student ran the university for a day
body: The Herald of 5 March 1996 printed Eva Farrar's own account of standing in for the university president, headlined "Day Was Not Boring for Farrar." SGA's minutes of 16 January and 13 February 1996 record the President for a Day contest as the association's business that spring.

src.label: Herald 71:44, 5 Mar 1996 - Farrar, "Day Was Not Boring for Farrar"

title: The Herald called SGA disproportionately Greek
body: During the election campaign the Herald ran Fred Lucas's report headlined "Student Government Association: Greeks Disproportional," on the share of the congress drawn from fraternities and sororities. It appeared in the same issue as coverage of construction costs and a campus film festival.

src.label: Herald 71:49, 2 Apr 1996 - Lucas, "Student Government Association: Greeks Disproportional"

title: SGA favoured a housing idea
body: The Herald of 5 September 1996 carried Kim Leonard's report headlined "Student Government Association Favors Housing Idea." The same issue carried Jason Hall's report that Provide-A-Ride hinged on student involvement.

src.label: Herald 72:5, 5 Sep 1996 - Leonard, "Student Government Association Favors Housing Idea"

title: Intramural facilities, t-shirts and the budget
body: The meeting of 10 September 1996 discussed intramural facilities, the coming elections, t-shirts, the budget and campus improvements. Intramural facilities carried over into the following week's meeting.

title: Diddle Park dedication and Focus on Western
body: The meeting of 21 October 1996 took up online services, the dedication of Diddle Park, Focus on Western, homecoming, drug abuse, shuttle service and legislation. It falls in the week of the Herald's Homecoming edition, which carried a feature on thirty years of student government.

title: Organizational aid, the Hillraisers and the computer labs
body: On 29 October 1996 the congress discussed homecoming, dining services, the Hillraisers, campus lighting, the budget, computer labs, shuttle services and organizational aid. It is the only record of organizational aid being handled in Kristen Miller's autumn.

title: An AIDS lecture and the banquet
body: The meeting of 13 November 1996 covered a banquet, summer financial aid, flags, an AIDS lecture, the budget, computer labs and legislation. World AIDS Day appears again in the minutes of 19 and 23 November, so the lecture belongs to SGA's preparation for 1 December.

title: AIDS Day, Bowl for Kids Sake and designated drivers
body: On 19 November 1996 the congress discussed elections, Bowl for Kids Sake, Provide-a-Ride, AIDS Day, vacancies, the budget, campus lighting, designated drivers and the website. Designated driver cards were funded a year later by Bill 97-3-F.

title: The ride plan was announced to start
body: The Herald of 21 November 1996 announced that the ride plan was set to begin, under Kim Leonard's byline. This is the notice of Provide-a-Ride's start rather than a report of how it ran; the Herald's assessment came the following February.

src.label: Herald 72:26, 21 Nov 1996 - Leonard, "Ride Plan Set to Begin"

title: A Christmas banquet and a residence hall task force
body: The last meeting of 1996, on 3 December, covered Bowl for Kid's Sake, a Christmas banquet, meeting attendance, vacancies, the budget, a residence hall task force, the bylaws, Provide-a-Ride, a digital telephone book, counselling, housing refunds, housing contracts and check cashing.

title: A plan to put SGA meetings on television
body: The Herald of 16 January 1997 reported that SGA planned to broadcast its meetings on television, under Matt Batcheldor's byline. The plan belongs to the same push for visibility as the website discussed in the January minutes.

src.label: Herald 72:30, 16 Jan 1997 - Batcheldor, "Student Government Association Plans to Broadcast Meetings on TV"

title: Designated driver cards and the Poland Hall computer lab
body: The meeting of 28 January 1997 discussed the Poland Hall computer lab, campus lighting, Provide-a-Ride, Bowl for Kids Sake, the budget, diversity, designated driver cards and email accounts. Designated drivers had first reached the minutes the previous November.

title: A diversity forum, and an executive council that met the same night
body: On 4 February 1997 the congress discussed Provide-a-Ride, the Academic Council, Healthy Toppers, vacancies, the budget, the Drug Council, a diversity forum and bike racks. The Executive Council met an hour later on memorial trees, a Judicial Council vacancy and Coming Home.

title: Thomas Meredith accepted a job in Alabama
body: The Herald of 6 February 1997 reported that president Thomas Meredith had accepted a position in Alabama. His departure set off the presidential search that SGA followed through the spring, taking a seat on the search committee under Resolution 97-4-S.

src.label: Herald 72:35, 6 Feb 1997 - Stamper, "Thomas Meredith Accepts Alabama Position"

title: Provide-a-Ride got high marks
body: Two and a half months after the service began, the Herald reported it was getting high marks, under Matt Batcheldor's byline. The report came a fortnight after the same paper had written that the programme needed SGA and student support to survive.

src.label: Herald 72:36, 11 Feb 1997 - Batcheldor, "Provide-a-Ride Gets high Marks"

title: Child care grants return to the agenda
body: The meeting of 18 February 1997 covered Provide-a-Ride, Thomas Meredith, dead week, the budget, an NAACP meeting, the bylaws, fire alarm keys and child care grants. The grants stayed on the agenda through 25 February and 4 March.

title: A Crimestoppers breakfast and a charity lockup
body: The meeting of 4 March 1997 discussed a Crimestoppers breakfast, a muscular dystrophy association lockup, child care grants, the budget, faculty evaluations, the presidential search, parking lots and vacancies. The same day the congress passed Resolution 97-4-S on the presidential search committee.

title: Bridging the Gap, a senior class gift and the spring clean-up
body: On 11 March 1997 the congress discussed elections, banquets, the senior class gift, dining services, the budget, faculty evaluations, the Bridging the Gap forum, Campus Clean Up, Pearce-Ford Tower safety and fax machines. Resolution 97-5-S on installing two fax machines on campus carries the same date.

title: A job fair, and the state's student body presidents
