body: The meeting of 1 April 1997 covered a memorial tree, the Kentucky student body presidents, the Bridging the Gap forum, the website, the budget, faculty evaluations, a job fair, Campus Clean Up, awards, fax machines and student seating at basketball games. Bill 97-4-S, funding two fax machines, carries the same date.

title: A student day at the baseball game
body: The meeting of 8 April 1997 discussed the memorial tree dedication, elections, a student day at a baseball game, vacancies, the budget, a drug programme, Campus Clean Up, student seating at basketball games and a request for an Easter holiday break. Resolution 97-12-S on the Easter break carries the same date.

title: Students called SGA elitist
body: Twelve days before the election the Herald ran Matt Batcheldor's report that students were questioning the association's "elitist attitude." It belongs to a run of complaints that year about how far SGA reached beyond its own membership.

src.label: Herald 72:50, 10 Apr 1997 - Batcheldor, "Students Question Student Government Association's Elitist Attitude, Concern"

title: Gary Ransdell got the top job
body: The Herald of 11 September 1997 reported that Gary Ransdell had been chosen as Western's president, ending the search SGA had followed since February. The Board of Regents, on which the student regent sits, approved his contract on 4 November and he took office the following week.

src.label: Herald 73:6, 11 Sep 1997 - Back, "Gary Ransdell Gets Top Job"

title: Organizational Aid paid out $6,200 in Coffman's first autumn
body: Bill 97-2-F, dated 28 October 1997, disbursed $6,200 to a listed set of student organizations. The same sum was budgeted for Organizational Aid again the following autumn, when Bill 98-9-F split it among forty-one groups.

title: The Academic Council amended SGA's no-test proposal
body: The Herald of 28 October 1997 reported that the Academic Council had amended the no-test proposal, under Charlie Lanter's byline. The dead week campaign had been running since Resolution 96-2-S of 20 February 1996, which asked for a reading week before finals.

src.label: Herald 73:18, 28 Oct 1997 - Lanter, "Academic Council Amends No-Test Proposal"

title: Sober drivers got free drinks
body: The Herald of 13 November 1997 reported that sober drivers were getting free drinks, under Charlie Lanter's byline, nine days after Bill 97-3-F funded designated driver cards. The cards were still being distributed the following February.

src.label: Herald 73:23, 13 Nov 1997 - Lanter, "Sober Drivers Get Free Drinks"

title: The Regents upheld the $5 student fee
body: The Herald of 3 February 1998 reported that the Board of Regents had upheld a $5 student fee, in coverage tying the decision to Detrex Field and the Student Government Association. The student regent sat on the board that took the vote.

src.label: Herald 73:32, 3 Feb 1998 - Felkins, "Regents Uphold $5 Student Fee"

title: A homecoming float committee was created
body: Bill 98-3-F, dated 6 October 1998, created a homecoming float committee. Two weeks later Bill 98-6-F funded the joint SGA and Hillraiser float itself.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 98-3-F, Creation of Homecoming Float Committee

title: Thirty ashtrays for the campus
body: Bill 98-7-F, dated 23 October 1998, authorised SGA to buy thirty ashtrays for campus. Cigarette receptacles had been an SGA request since Resolution 93-3-F on sand barrels five years earlier.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 98-7-F, Placing Ashtrays Outside Residence Halls & Campus Buildings

title: A weekend activities survey
body: Bill 98-8-F, dated 26 October 1998, provided for a survey of weekend activities. The congress was under public pressure that autumn over what it did, and answered the charge directly in the Herald in December.

title: Orientation made mandatory for new members
body: Bill 98-11-F, dated 30 November 1998, proposed mandatory SGA orientation for incoming members. It was filed in the same week as the Bookswap.com sponsorship and the 1999 Camp Fair funding.

title: An open forum for students
body: Bill 99-5-S, dated 16 February 1999, provided for an open forum for students. Public forums had been SGA business since Bill 94-9-F established a series of them in 1994.

title: SGA officers written onto the University Center Board
body: Bill 99-13-S, dated 23 March 1999, amended the SGA constitution to make officers representatives on the University Center Board, the body that programmed campus entertainment. It passed in the same session as the child care grants and the KASWE conference funding.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 99-13-S, SGA Representatives to University Center Board

title: The Herald reported SGA bending its election rules
body: The Herald of 6 April 1999 reported that SGA had bent its election rules, under Ryan Clark's byline. The disputed spring election ran on through a recount and a Judicial Council ruling that overturned the result later that month.

src.label: Herald 74:48, 6 Apr 1999 - Clark, "Student Government Association Bends Election Rules"

title: Organizational aid disbursed for Coates's autumn
body: Bill 99-15-F, dated 26 October 1999, disbursed funds to student organizations. It is the only record of the autumn organizational aid round in Amanda Coates's year.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 99-15-F, Disbursement Student Government Association Organizational Aid

title: Suggestion boxes in the residence halls
body: Bill 99-14-F, dated 9 November 1999, provided for suggestion boxes to be installed in the residence halls. The idea outlasted the administration: SGA legislated a slip holder for the boxes in 2001 and more boxes in 2002.

title: Website guidelines written into the constitution
body: A bill dated 6 December 1999 amended the SGA constitution to include guidelines for the association's website. It is filed in SGA's records without a number, as Bill 99- -F.

title: Insurance put SGA on edge
body: The Herald of 2 March 2000 reported that insurance had put the Student Government Association on edge, under Rex Hall's byline. The archive holds only the article's title and byline, and nothing further about which policy was at issue.

src.label: Herald 75:43, 2 Mar 2000 - Hall, "Insurance Puts Student Government Association on Edge"

title: SGA opposed a dining services building
body: The Herald of 20 April 2000 reported that SGA opposed a dining services building, under Abbey Brown's byline. The same issue carried Rex Hall's report that SGA membership was still declining.

src.label: Herald 75:54, 20 Apr 2000 - Brown, "Student Government Association Opposes Building"

title: Civic engagement bracelets and Katrina relief opened the year
body: The earliest 2005-06 meeting in the SGA collection, on 6 September 2005, was convened to discuss elections, the retreat, Hurricane Katrina and Civic Engagement bracelets. The bracelets appear again in the minutes of 20 September and 1 November 2005.

title: Campus Safety Walk and Provide-A-Ride carried into a new year
body: At its second meeting of the autumn the senate discussed the retreat, the Campus Safety Walk, the athletics committee and Provide-A-Ride. Provide-A-Ride appears again in the minutes of 4 October 2005.

title: SGA screened Living with Cancer and began a documentary series
body: The senate discussed the Living with Cancer documentary at its meeting of 11 October 2005, alongside Listen Up Legislators, homecoming and Dialogue Day. An SGA documentary is recorded in the minutes of 4 and 18 October and a documentary series in those of 25 October.

title: Dialogue Day put students in a room with administrators
body: Dialogue Day appears in three consecutive sets of senate minutes in October 2005 as a programme SGA was organising, alongside the documentary series and Listen Up Legislators. SGA returned to it the following year in Resolution 03-06-F of 2 October 2006, catalogued as proposing a day for students to meet administrators.

title: SGA organised a forum for transfer students
body: The 25 October 2005 senate meeting covered Dialogue Day, the documentary series, Listen Up Legislators and a transfer student forum. The forum recurs in the minutes of 8 November and 29 November 2005 and 14 February 2006, making it a sustained programme rather than a single evening.

title: Senate took up library hours for finals week
body: At its last meeting of the autumn semester the senate discussed the banquet, library hours for finals week, and legislation. Extended library hours during finals became a recurring SGA concern; a bill of April 2007 proposed SGA funding for them.

title: Senators moved to censure President Katie Dawson
body: The Herald of 7 March 2006 reported that SGA senators would ask the Judicial Council to censure President Katie Dawson. The same issue carried two opinion pieces on the organisation, one asking whether student government was missing in action and one arguing it should be improved. The archive records no outcome to the censure move beyond its delay two days later.

title: Senators delayed the censure decision
body: Two days after the move became public the Herald reported that SGA senators had delayed a decision on censuring President Katie Dawson. No later issue in the digitised run records the matter being resolved.

title: Campus Cleanup ran on 9 March 2006
body: The senate had discussed campus cleanup at its 7 March 2006 meeting, and the Herald of 9 March carried the item Campus CleanUp Today, reporting the event as happening that day rather than announcing it in advance. SGA's own website later said the clean-up traced its roots to Henry Hardin Cherry's presidency and that SGA sponsored it each year.

title: Senate weighed an education funding rally and an SGA archivist
body: The 7 March 2006 senate meeting covered a Why Kentucky Education is Important rally, the campus cleanup, and the creation of an archivist position within SGA.

title: Presidential candidates agreed on most issues at the spring forum
body: The senate had scheduled a presidential debate at its 28 March 2006 meeting, and the Herald of 4 April reported that the SGA candidates agreed on many issues. The same issue reported that seniors might be exempted from the new $46 student fee.

title: SGA still had $30,000 unspent with two weeks of term left
body: The Herald of 2 May 2006 reported that the SGA budget had $30,000 remaining. The same issue carried a column arguing the Herald was not responsible for the lack of enthusiasm for student government on campus.

title: SGA entered a team in Up 'til Dawn
body: Bill 06-03-F proposed that SGA sponsor a team in Up 'til Dawn. The senate minutes of 12 September 2006 record Up 'til Dawn and Habitat for Humanity being discussed together among the autumn's commitments.

title: Campus Cleanup set for 16 October and advertised on Facebook
body: Bill 04-06-F proposed 16 October 2006 as campus cleanup day. A companion bill, 05-06-F of 26 September, asked for an advertisement on Facebook to promote it. Both are proposals; the minutes of 10 and 17 October show the clean-up still being worked on but do not report how it went.

title: Dialogue Day revived with $800 behind it
body: Resolution 03-06-F of 2 October 2006 proposed a Dialogue Day at which students could meet university administrators, and Bill 08-06-F requested $800 to host it. Dialogue Day had been organised the previous autumn, when it ran through three sets of October 2005 minutes.

title: Organizational aid of $30,000 went out to student groups
body: Bill 06-06-F proposed disbursing $30,000 in organizational aid to a listed set of student organisations. The archive holds both readings, and the catalogue notes that the list of organisations in the first reading differs from the second, so groups were added or dropped between the two.

title: Buy-a-Book put $2,000 of book scholarships into students' hands
body: Bill 10-06-F proposed $2,000 in book scholarships for the spring 2007 semester. The programme left a full paper trail: a broadside advertising it, a press release announcing the 2006 winners on 1 December, and the form letter used to award them on 7 December. The senate renewed it for the following autumn on 27 February 2007.

title: Buy-a-Book winners announced by press release
body: SGA issued a press release on 1 December 2006 announcing the winners of that year's Buy-a-Book scholarships. A form letter used to award the scholarships is dated 7 December, and a broadside advertising the programme survives from the same week.

title: A resolution on vending machine prices reached a fifth reading
body: Resolution 09-06-F asked the university to reset vending machine prices. The archive holds its second reading and a revised fifth reading, both dated 24 November 2006, and the minutes of 5 December record it being tabled for want of quorum.

title: Senate asked for library serials funding to be restored
body: Resolution 04-06-F requested the restoration of library funding for serials, one of a run of academic-side measures that autumn. A report on the amount and cost of printing in the student technology computer labs survives from the same month.

title: SGA Week established by resolution
body: Resolution 02-07-S established a Student Government Association Week. SGA Week appears in the minutes of 27 February, 20 March, 27 March and 3 April 2007 as the officers organised it, and again in those of 25 March and 30 September 2008, so the resolution created a fixture rather than a one-off.

title: Dollies for Dorms bought moving equipment for residence halls
body: Bill 05-07-S proposed establishing an SGA Dollies for Dorms programme, buying dollies for students to use moving in and out of the residence halls.

title: Senate created Professor and Advisor of the Year awards
body: Bill 06-07-S proposed awards for professor and advisor of the year. It came in the same meeting as Dollies for Dorms and the spring campus clean-up resolution, in a session the minutes record as also covering professor accountability and a planned sit-in at a Regents meeting.

title: Spring campus clean-up set for 29 March 2007
body: Resolution 03-07-S proposed a campus clean up on 29 March 2007. This is the announcement rather than the event; the minutes of 20 March record the clean-up being organised but no later minutes report what happened on the day.

title: SGA created study abroad and field trip scholarships
body: Bill 07-07-S proposed an SGA study abroad scholarship and Bill 08-07-S proposed funding field trip scholarships. Both application forms survive in the archive dated the same day, so the programmes were built and opened rather than merely voted. They were still running when SGA described its services in 2009.

title: Study abroad scholarships proposed to be named for Caitlin Hammaren
body: Resolution 07-07-S proposed that the SGA study abroad scholarships be named in honour of Caitlin Hammaren, a Virginia Tech student killed in the April 2007 shooting. The senate had discussed the shooting at its meeting of 17 April, a week earlier.

title: SGA paid to keep the library open longer during finals week
body: Bill 11-07-S proposed SGA funding to extend library hours during finals week. The senate had discussed finals-week library hours as far back as December 2005; this is the first surviving measure putting SGA money behind it, and the Herald reported Helm-Cravens Library staying open later during finals week in April 2008.

title: Senate bought scantrons and blue books for exams
body: Bill 12-07-S proposed the purchase of scantron forms and blue books for student exams. SGA was still running the service in September 2009, when its website reported the senate approving 1,000 scantrons and 500 blue books for free distribution across campus.

title: Senate backed the Outlet Resource Center
body: Resolution 07-07-S proposed support for the Outlet Resource Center, described in the archive's catalogue as a safe haven for Western's gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgendered and questioning students. The same meeting took a resolution proposing a child care facility on or near campus for faculty and staff.

title: SGA printed a broadside for the plus-minus grading protest
body: A surviving SGA broadside promoted a plus/minus grading protest held in the Garrett Hall ballroom. The senate minutes of 20 March 2007 record a planned sit-in at a Board of Regents meeting, and those of 27 March record the protest itself being organised. The provost dropped the grading proposal that April.

title: SGA held an autumn cookout
body: The senate minutes of 9 and 16 October 2007 both record a cookout being organised, alongside Walk-Out Western. The minutes name the event but record nothing about how it went.

title: SGA planned a finals week Oasis and a holiday dinner
body: The executive council minutes of 13 November 2007 record the finals week oasis being planned along with cafeteria hours and computer labs. The senate minutes of 27 November carry it forward together with a holiday dinner, and those of 4 December record the oasis again. The following April the senate voted $250 for a Spring Oasis, then in its second year.

title: Senate worked on an end-of-semester study day
body: An end-of-semester study day appears in the senate minutes of 9 October and 6 November 2007 and in the executive council minutes of the same date, alongside homecoming and Walk-Out Western. It returned in the spring, appearing in the minutes of 1 April 2008.

title: Gatton Academy students asked for a seat in SGA
body: The executive cabinet minutes of 24 March 2008 record a discussion of Gatton Academy students participating in SGA, alongside plus/minus grading, the Hall of Distinguished Seniors and a block party. The Herald of 27 March carried an article headed that the Gatton Academy of Math and Science wanted representation too.

title: The Herald turned its opinion page on SGA during the election
body: The Herald of 27 March 2008 ran an editorial cartoon depicting SGA as clowns, an editorial saying the organisation needed to change its election process, and rival opinion pieces from candidates Johnathon Boles and from Theodore Harden, Kevin Smiley and Reagan Gilley. On 8 April a further cartoon and an editorial headed that SGA needed an overhaul followed.

title: Skylar Jordan filed a complaint against the Red Towel Party
body: The Herald of 8 April 2008 reported that Skylar Jordan had filed a complaint against the Red Towel Party, the slate that had campaigned to energise SGA. Two days later the paper reported the Judicial Council was addressing both a tie and the campaign complaint, and that SGA would have to elect a new Speaker of the Senate. The archive does not record how the council ruled.

title: Spring campus clean-up rescheduled to Thursday
body: The Herald of 8 April 2008 reported that SGA had rescheduled the campus clean-up for Thursday. The senate minutes of 25 March and 1 April both record the clean-up being organised.

title: Western won the national ONE Campus Challenge
body: The Herald of 10 April 2008 reported that Western had won the ONE Campus Challenge, the national campaign against extreme poverty and global AIDS. SGA had introduced legislation asking the senate to recognise Western as a ONE Campus at its first spring meeting on 29 January, and the Herald of 24 April reported ONE leaders advocating an education bill in Washington.

title: The Ruckus free music bill was shelved over IT concerns
body: The Herald of 24 April 2008 reported that the Ruckus bill had been shelved because of information technology concerns, a week after the senate was due to consider it.

title: Senate rejected a diploma proposal and backed the SEAT
body: The Herald of 24 April 2008 reported that SGA had rejected a diploma proposal and that it was in favour of the Student Engagement Activities Transcript, the record of learning outside the classroom that SGA was still promoting to students in 2009. The same issue reported Helm-Cravens Library staying open later during finals week.

title: A Nappy Roots concert came before the senate
body: The senate minutes of 16 September 2008 record a Nappy Roots concert on the agenda alongside football games, Western Wednesdays and appointments, and the minutes of 23 September record it again together with the campus safety walk and Buy-a-Book. The archive shows the concert being arranged; it does not record whether it took place or what it cost.

title: Western Wednesdays began as an SGA programme
body: Western Wednesdays appears in the senate minutes of 16 and 23 September 2008. By March 2010 SGA was running Western Wednesdays as a discount scheme rewarding students for wearing Western apparel in Bowling Green, with twenty-two participating businesses.

title: SGA Week, homecoming and campus cleanup day set for the autumn
body: The senate meeting of 30 September 2008 was given over to SGA Week, homecoming and campus cleanup day. Homecoming returns in the minutes of 21 and 28 October and 3 November, so it occupied the senate for more than a month.

title: SGA ran a mock election before the 2008 presidential vote
body: The senate minutes of 7 October 2008 record a mock election alongside organizational aid and Buy-a-Book. SGA had run a mock gubernatorial election with the Secretary of State's office the previous autumn, in which 127 students voted.

title: Senate took up the 22 October campus lockdown
body: The senate minutes of 28 October 2008 record a discussion of the lock down of campus on 22 October, together with homecoming, Buy-a-Book scholarships and committee appointments. The Herald of 23 October carried a timeline of events, an article headed that gunfire was unconfirmed and the investigation continuing, and a piece reporting the university pleased with its emergency response.

title: Senate resolved in support of an emergency communications system
body: Resolution 01-08-F was a resolution in support of a crisis management system for the university. It came five days after shots were reported outside Pearce-Ford Tower and six weeks before the October campus lockdown.

title: Scholar Development grants opened with $12,000 behind them
body: SGA's Academic Affairs committee and the Director of Academic and Student Affairs were allotted $12,000 to spend on scholarships for the student body, covering textbooks, study abroad, field trips and research conferences. The Scholar Development Grant application, posted on 16 November 2009, let a student apply for $250 at a time up to $500 in an academic year, for professional conferences, research equipment and research expenses. Dave Vickery chaired the committee.

src.label: WKU SGA website, Scholar Development Grant post, 16 November 2009 (Wayback)

title: Senate bought 1,000 scantrons and 500 blue books for students to take free
body: In September 2009 the Student Senate approved the purchase of 1,000 scantron forms and 500 blue books. SGA then placed them free of charge in the fifteen residence halls, the Gatton Academy, the SGA office and the computer labs in Helm Library and Mass Media and Technology Hall. The service went back to a bill of April 2007.

src.label: WKU SGA website, About page, November 2009 (Wayback)

title: Western Wednesdays announced with twenty-three Bowling Green businesses
body: SGA announced that its Western Wednesdays discount programme would begin on 17 March 2010, rewarding students who showed a WKU ID while wearing Western apparel. The published list ran to twenty-two businesses, from half-price sandwiches at Jimmy John's and 25 percent off at Hog Wild BBQ to a $3.99 daily buffet at Cici's Pizza for a year. This is SGA's own announcement before the start date, not a report of how the scheme ran.
money: discounts of 10 to 25 percent at 23 businesses

src.label: WKU SGA website, Student Discounts page, March 2010 (Wayback)

title: SGA study abroad scholarship applications opened
body: SGA announced on 18 November 2009 that its study abroad scholarship was available, describing it as competitive and administered on a rolling basis. The scholarship had been created by a bill in March 2007 and proposed that April to be named for Caitlin Hammaren.

src.label: WKU SGA website, Study Abroad Scholarship post, 18 November 2009 (Wayback)

title: Organizational aid ran to more than $40,000 a year
body: SGA described organizational aid as providing over $40,000 a year to campus organisations, with each organisation able to apply for up to $500. Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman was the contact and the application was posted on the SGA site.
money: over $40,000 a year, capped at $500 per organisation

src.label: WKU SGA website, About page, November 2009 (Wayback)

title: SGA joined National Make A Difference Week
body: SGA announced on 30 September 2009 that it was taking part in National Make A Difference Week at Western, a week of causes and fundraisers. It named Habitat for Humanity, Relay for Life, Up 'til Dawn, Volunteering in Progress and United Way Worldwide as partners in the effort.

title: Provide-A-Ride came back into service
body: SGA posted on 30 September 2009 that the Provide-A-Ride service was active again. The free late-night ride home, available from 10 p.m. to 2 a.m. Tuesday to Saturday on production of a current WKU ID, had been suspended earlier that month when the contract with the previous operator ended.

title: Issues Awareness Week ran on the Hill
body: SGA announced Issues Awareness Week on the Hill for 30 November to 4 December 2009. The announcement was posted on 28 November; the archive holds no later account of the week itself.

title: Hall of Distinguished Seniors opened for autumn 2009
body: SGA extended the deadline for its autumn 2009 Hall of Distinguished Seniors applications on 12 November, to 2 p.m. the following Monday. SGA's website described the award as the highest recognition given to graduates by the student body.

title: Cage the Elephant played to several thousand on South Lawn
body: SGA and the Campus Activities Board co-sponsored a free outdoor show on South Lawn on the Wednesday night, with Manchester Orchestra also on the bill. The hour-long set was nearly shut down halfway through when the crowd pressed the front guard rail hard enough that singer Matt Shultz was asked to warn people back, telling them legs were being broken. The concert doubled as the launch party for the Starry Nights Music Festival, which had been cancelled that year, and its founder Bryan Graves worked the front of the stage holding the gate up and pulling out crowd surfers.
money: several thousand in the crowd, by the promoter's estimate

title: SGA announced a DUC forum for the day the regents saw the plans
body: At the 27 September 2011 meeting SGA said it would host an unveiling of the Downing University Center renovation plans at DUC from 11:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., following the Board of Regents meeting that Friday at which the plans were to be shown. It was to be set up as a forum so students could learn about the renovation. This is what was announced; the Herald report was printed before the event and does not say how it went.

title: The Purple Line got a third bus after carrying close to 20,000 riders
body: The Safe Ride shuttle SGA had created with Parking and Transportation in 2012 to replace Provide-A-Ride, known on campus as the Purple Line, entered its second year with a third bus added. Transit manager Stephen Rowland said SGA wanted to keep the line's 15-minute run time and the extra bus was needed to hold the schedule across 16 stops and a 45-minute circuit, and that the line had carried close to 20,000 passengers in its first year. The line ran Thursday, Friday and Saturday from 10 p.m. to 2 a.m. Driver Quinten Haynie said Homecoming week and the opening weeks of class were the busiest.
money: close to 20,000 passengers in its first year

title: Nicki Seay ran unopposed as SGA's homecoming queen candidate
body: At the first meeting after the fall election, the senate nominated and voted on its homecoming queen candidate. Administrative Vice President Nicki Seay was nominated, ran unopposed and took the nomination. The same meeting swore in fifteen new senators and heard that the Campus Improvements Committee was developing a community garden with GreenToppers.

title: Preston Center memberships cut in half for sixty part-time students
body: The senate passed Funding for the Preston Membership Voucher Program, allocating $1,050 so that 60 part-time students could buy a semester membership to the Preston Center at half price. The semester fee for part-time students was $35, and a voucher brought it down to $17.50. It was one of two voucher bills passed that night.

title: Fifty ID vouchers, restricted to students who had not lost a card
body: After suspending its bylaws to take the bill the same night, the senate passed Funding for the Identification Vouchers Program, allocating $500 to cover half the $20 cost of a WKU ID card for 50 students. The voucher was available only to students who had not previously lost an ID card.
money: $500 covering half the cost of 50 cards

title: Transcript vouchers handed out first come, first served
body: Bill 3-14-F was the only bill to pass that night, allocating $500 to a programme covering the $7 cost of an official transcript request for 60 students, two vouchers to a student. Academic Affairs Committee Chair Josh Knight, who wrote the bill, said $7 might not seem much but some students could not carry the extra expense, and that SGA would consider adding vouchers if demand required it.

title: A thirty-nine dollar sticker survey asked students what to fix
body: Bill 4-14-F allocated about $39 from legislative discretionary funds to the Campus Improvements Committee for flip charts and multi-coloured dots, to be used in a walk-up survey asking students what they wanted improved on campus. Author Elizabeth McGrew, a Henderson graduate student, said online surveys took too much of students' time and drew fewer responses than a visible one would.
money: about $39 for flip charts and dot stickers

title: Study Away scholarships funded at $1,200 for a second year
body: Bill 6-14-F passed with no debate, allocating $1,200 from Academic Affairs Committee funding for additional scholarships for students applying to Study Away, the programme for travel within the United States rather than abroad. Committee chair Joshua Knight said the same amount had been given the previous year and had been used up, so the committee thought it fair to repeat it.
money: $1,200, the same as the year before

title: SGA picked its director of public relations as homecoming nominee
body: At the same meeting SGA voted Director of Public Relations KJ Hall as its 2014 Homecoming nominee, and swore in newly elected senators.

title: Student Legal Services Clinic opened with an SGA resolution behind it
body: WKU's Student Legal Services Clinic was set to open on Friday 30 January in Tate Page Hall room 252, after four years of on-and-off preparation by paralegal studies professor Julie Shadoan. It was open to all students including part-time, transfer, international and regional campus students, drew on about twelve volunteer attorneys, and charged $30 an hour against roughly $300 an hour for an average attorney. SGA President Nicki Taylor said SGA had passed a resolution supporting the clinic and the creation of a $4 student fee to pay for an in-house attorney.
money: $30 an hour against about $300 for an average attorney

title: Five hundred dollars to promote the Community Farmers Market
body: Bill 4-15-S, Funding to Support the Community Farmers Market, passed unanimously and without debate, allocating $500 from legislative discretionary funds to the Office of Sustainability to promote the market to students. Co-author Brian Chism said the point was to let students know what food options were available to them.

title: Senate passed a $138,500 budget for the year
body: The SGA budget for the year was passed at $138,500 at the same meeting that swore in three new senators and approved the Preston and identification voucher programmes. Seats remained open and election applications were due 15 September.

title: Senate asked WKU to let unused meal swipes roll over
body: Resolution 5-14-F passed with no debate, supporting an amendment to university dining policy so that meal swipes left at the end of a week could carry forward as meal plans or meal plan dollars rather than being forfeited on Sunday. Author William Berry said students paid for those swipes and should not lose them. He said Aramark was running a feasibility test on whether meal plan prices would have to rise to make a rollover work.

title: Both attempts to change discretionary funding died at the final meeting
body: At the last meeting of the spring the senate took up two competing approaches to Legislative Discretionary Aid. Resolution 11-15-S by Senator Jody Dahmer, which would have stopped SGA giving discretionary money directly to individual students and organisations and pushed them to the Organizational Aid Committee, failed 11-7 for want of a two-thirds majority; Dahmer argued that without a system, senators could end up promising kickbacks for votes, while Senator Josh Knight opposed any blanket ban on recognising special cases. Bill 15-15-S, which would have split the remaining discretionary money between five organisations that had missed the organizational aid deadline, tied 7-7 and Speaker of the Senate Jay Todd Richey broke the tie against it.

title: Sustainability Day filled 28 October from breakfast to dinner
body: Sustainability Committee Chairwoman Chelsea Faught told the senate that Sustainability Day was approaching, a series of events across campus on 28 October. It was to open with breakfast at 8 a.m. in Downing Student Union, run a GreenToppers pumpkin carving outside the bookstore from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., include a talk by President Gary Ransdell in Ransdell Hall and a scavenger hunt in the Music Hall from 3 to 5 p.m., and close with a dinner and music at the Augenstein Alumni Center. This is the programme as announced; the Herald report was printed before the day.

title: Listening tours announced for the three regional campuses
body: President Jay Todd Richey told the senate that SGA would take listening tours to WKU's extended campuses in mid-November: Glasgow on 10 November at 11:30 a.m., Owensboro on 11 November at 2 p.m. and Elizabethtown/Fort Knox on 12 November at noon. He said he would use them to hear students' issues and concerns and what SGA could do about them, and that all students were welcome. This is what was announced; the report predates the tours.

title: A thousand dollars set aside for the fiftieth anniversary celebration
body: Bill 1-16-S, Funding for the 50th Anniversary Celebration of WKU SGA, was approved with no debate, allocating $1,000 for a celebration to be held on 30 April 2016 at the Augenstein Alumni Center. Senator Nathan Cherry of the Campus Improvements Committee said SGA had been on campus since 1966 and that an anniversary that comes round once deserved some kind of celebration.

title: Sixty-four dollars of posters for a film showing and a race forum
body: Bill 2-16-S passed with no debate, allocating $64.30 from senate discretionary funds for posters advertising two MyCampusToo events: a co-sponsored showing of the film Bamboozled in Cherry Hall room 227 on 17 February, and a forum titled Dear White People/Dear Black People, Life and Race on the Hill in the SGA chambers on 24 February. The bill is the record of what was booked; the Herald report predates both events.

title: Identification and Preston vouchers renewed at $650 between them
body: Two long-running voucher programmes were refunded the same night, both without debate. Bill 3-16-S put $300 towards identification vouchers to partially cover the $20 cost of a new WKU ID card. Bill 4-16-S allocated $350 from legislative discretionary funding for Preston Center vouchers, enough for 20 part-time students to have half of their semester membership fee paid.
money: $300 for ID vouchers and $350 for 20 Preston vouchers

title: Water bottles rescued for WellU Wednesdays and the Earth Day festival
body: Bill 7-16-S was approved with no debate, allocating $300 to cover half the cost of water bottles that had been ordered for an earlier event but arrived late because of a manufacturing problem. Author Chelsea Faught said the bill simply changed what the bottles were for: they would now be handed out at WellU Wednesdays starting 30 March and at the 2016 Earth Day Festival.
money: $300, half the cost of the bottles

title: Nineteen dollars of posters for an LGBTQIA forum
body: Bill 11-16-S was approved with no debate, allocating $19.29 for 30 posters advertising a forum titled Life as an LGBTQIA Student on the Hill. MyCampusToo was to sponsor the forum in the SGA Senate Chambers on Wednesday 30 March, on what campus life was like for lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex and asexual students. The bill records what was booked; the report predates the forum.

title: Four hundred dollars for Pakistan Day
body: Bill 12-16-S, Funding for Pakistan Day Cosponsored by Pakistani Student Association and MyCampusToo, was approved with no debate. It allocated $400 to the Pakistani Student Association to cover traditional food, printed flyers and posters, decorations, utensils and prizes for the event.

title: Senate refused to sponsor a charity 5K
body: Bill 13-16-S would have given $200 to Phi Sigma Phi to sponsor a student-led charity 5K in exchange for promotional items and credit, with the proceeds going to the Hugh O'Brian Youth Leadership Foundation. Author J. William Berry said all proceeds would reach the charity. The bill was defeated after senators argued that discretionary funds were the wrong source and that the run was already collecting donations from many other organisations.

title: Almost 900 students voted in a fall election with nearly 70 candidates
body: Voting for the SGA senate ran on TopNet on 17 and 18 September, with almost 900 students casting ballots among nearly 70 candidates. SGA held a results party in the Senate Chambers, and the counts came in about fifteen minutes past midnight on 19 September. Student Body President Stephen Mayer called the turnout amazing. Seven senators at large, three freshman senators and an Intercultural Student Engagement Center senator were seated.
money: almost 900 votes cast for nearly 70 candidates

title: A hundred and fifty dollars of Subway for the campus safety walk
body: Bill 15-18-F passed, allocating $150 for Subway catering at the WKU Campus Safety Walk set for 14 November. The Herald report was printed before the walk and says only what was funded.

title: A hundred dollars for a Sustainability Day basket
body: Bill 17-18-F, written by Sustainability Committee Chair Jayden Thomas, passed 32-1 and put $100 towards a basket for Sustainability Day on 14 November, sponsored jointly by SGA and its Sustainability Committee. This records the funding; the report predates the day itself.

title: Twenty-four SGA members went to the Rally for Higher Education
body: SGA sent 24 members, the executive board and selected senators, to the annual Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort, joining delegations from Murray State and other universities across the Commonwealth. The WKU delegation was led by Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds, who said higher education was not just about students but about culture and communities. Director of Information Technology Paul Brosky said he hoped the students would be heard by legislators. The Herald report was printed on the morning of the rally.

title: Second Unite for Fairness night filled DSU with handwritten letters
body: SGA and the Queer Student Union held the second Unite for Fairness event in Downing Student Union, where students wrote letters to Bowling Green city commissioners in support of a fairness ordinance. State Representative and WKU history professor Patti Minter, a member of the Bowling Green fairness movement since 1999, gave a presentation on its history before students began writing. SGA Director of Public Relations Noah Moore, who had helped organise the first event the previous semester, said a handwritten letter would reach a commissioner more than an email or a phone call.

title: Two hundred and fifty dollars for Lavender Graduation
body: Bill 25-19-S passed 25-0, allocating $250 for Lavender Graduation, the ceremony recognising the achievements of LGBT graduates and their allies. The money covered stoles, decorations and food.

title: Women's Forum funding doubled on the floor to $200
body: Bill 28-19-S came to the floor asking $100 for the upcoming Women's Forum and was friendly amended to $200, half from the food budget and half from the senate discretionary fund, and to add buttons alongside the brownies, cookies and light refreshments. It passed 25-0.

title: Two justices confirmed and six spending bills passed in one night
body: With President Stephen Mayer absent ill and his report read by Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds, the senate confirmed Erika Puhakka as an associate justice 27-0 and Isaac Keller, the longest-serving member of the Judicial Council at two years, as chief justice 28-0. Six spending bills followed, among them Bill 22-19-S giving $1,700 in organizational aid to eight groups, Bill 24-19-S giving $500 to Blaq Art Nouveau for a Carpe Diem recruiting event, Bill 27-19-S giving $75 to the Queer Student Union for bracelet-making materials it had been unable to request in time because its advisor changed, and Bill 26-19-S reserving $108 to book indoor tables in case it rained on Earth Day.
money: six spending bills in one sitting

title: Fifty-three SGA scholarships awarded in one bill
body: Bill 29-19-S passed 25-0, funding the scholarships SGA awarded that year. Director of Academic and Student Affairs Aubrey Kelley presented them: 27 summer term scholarships totalling $8,100, 18 study abroad and student teach abroad scholarships of $300 each totalling $5,400, and eight first-generation student scholarships of $250 each totalling $2,000. The Herald headlined the bill as allocating $17,000.

title: Earth Day festival moved indoors and packed Downing Student Union
body: SGA organised WKU's annual Earth Day festival on the Thursday, moving it from Centennial Mall into Downing Student Union. Sustainability Committee member Jayden Thomas said the committee expected about 60 organisations to table, with live music in the DSU Auditorium. SGA's own table let attendees paint small flower pots, the Horticulture Club gave away potted plants, and the Bowling Green Fairness Campaign tabled alongside, with founding member and state Representative Patti Minter attending to support what she called intersectional justice.

title: SGA sponsored the third Bowling Green Pride Festival
body: Bill 2-19-F allocated $500 from senate discretionary funding to sponsor the Bowling Green Pride Festival held on 5 October 2019 at Circus Square Park by the Bowling Green Fairness group. The money bought a Silver Sponsorship, putting SGA's name and logo on the festival t-shirt and website and securing tabling space for the Committee for Diversity and Inclusion. The bill's authors, senators Conner Hounshell and Mark Clark, wrote that funding was necessary because LGBTQ+ students were not legally protected in Bowling Green for want of a Fairness ordinance, and noted this was the third such festival and that SGA had sponsored every one before it. The posted form records a first reading on 3 September 2019, a second reading on 10 September and a passing vote.

title: Judicial Council filled out with four nominations
body: The senate confirmed four nominees to the SGA Judicial Council at the 24 September 2019 meeting, filling the body out ahead of that week's senate elections. President Will Harris had interviewed freshman Jason Herlick, junior Derek Collins, sophomore Turner Reynolds and freshman Holden Schroeder before the meeting, and all four brought experience from other student government organisations. Herlick was confirmed unanimously after Senator Anthony Survance asked whether he had read SGA's constitution and rules. Collins, who headed WKU's Students Demand Action chapter, spoke about the council's duty to hold the association to account.

title: Diversity scholarship bill postponed over a Title IX conflict
body: Discussion of Bill 4-19-F, which would have created a diversity scholarship, was postponed at the 15 October 2019 meeting because the bill conflicted with Title IX, and no date was set for taking it up again while the Legislative Research Committee worked through it. At the same meeting Senator Symone Whalin announced a campus survey on the use of racial slurs and tried to show a clip from a slur-awareness video, which failed on technical grounds and was held over. Harris told senators he and Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds had met administrators about the special projects fund and come away with costings.

Study Away sends WKU students to placements elsewhere in the United States rather than abroad, and the office had approached SGA to keep the arrangement going. body: SGA offered students free transport to the Rally for Higher Education at the state Capitol on 3 March 2020, with WKU attendees leaving Diddle Arena at 6 a.m. About 400 students from Kentucky's public, private and technical institutions were expected to fill the Capitol rotunda between 10 a.m. and noon. The rally is organised through the Board of Student Body Presidents, and President Will Harris said WKU's agenda was pension reform, increases under the performance-based budget model and asset preservation funding. body: Bill 7-20-S proposed allocating $1,000 from senate discretionary funding to create a scholarship for students with financial need from Kentucky counties with low college graduation rates or a low share of residents holding bachelor's degrees. The bill argued those educational disparities track with lower incomes and higher unemployment and poverty, and directed the Director and Committee of Academic and Student Affairs to build an application identifying qualifying counties from data sources such as the Kentucky Council on Postsecondary Education. title: A thousand dollars to the food pantry after the campus closed

President Will Harris also said this year had seen the highest turnout for senate seats, more than he had seen in four years in SGA, and the meeting announced the town hall for 24 September at 7.30 p.m. in the DSU Auditorium, with elections on TopNet on 28 and 29 September. title: Federal judge dismissed the former president's suit against WKU
body: U.S. District Court Judge David Hale dismissed the federal claims in the lawsuit brought by a former SGA president against WKU on 2 March 2021 and remanded the remainder to state court. The suit, filed in 2018, individually named President Timothy Caboni, General Counsel Andrea Anderson and Director of Student Activities Charley Pride, and alleged the university's response to on-campus harassment she reported violated Title IX and 42 U.S. Code. The court found WKU was not aware of the harassment until February 2018, when her residence hall director reported it to the Title IX office, and granted the three named officials qualified immunity after finding no constitutional violation was proved. The university had called the accusations maliciously untrue when the suit was filed; her attorney declined to comment on the dismissal.

The Herald published the ballot: candidates stood for senator-at-large, the class seats, the first-generation seat, the Gatton Academy seat and the college seats, with Avery Wells and Reed Breunig running for administrative vice president and Wells also standing for a senate seat. title: A lobbyist and former Tennessee legislator spoke to the senate

title: A Dress for Success drive for clothes, shoes and toiletries
body: Bill 11-24-S allocated $800 from the legislative discretionary fund to the Community Relations Committee's Dress for Success drive, buying shoes, socks, underwear and toiletries. Students could add donations at the SGA front desk between 29 February and 5 April 2024, earning service hours in proportion to what they gave up to a cap of five. The goods went to the Gordon Ford College of Business professional clothes closet and to the family resource coordinators of the city and county schools. The bill was read a second time on 27 February 2024.

title: Spring Fling, a tailgate on South Lawn for Kids Cancer Alliance
body: Bill 15-24-S allocated $450 from the legislative discretionary budget to an SGA Spring Fling on South Lawn on 27 March 2024, with $250 buying complimentary tailgate food from Gordon Food Service and $200 funding two $100 scholarships. All money raised at the event went to Kids Cancer Alliance. The bill was authored by senators Madison Payne and Ryan Dilts and read a second time on 12 March 2024; the posted form leaves the vote line blank.

title: SGA joined Hope Harbor for Denim Day
body: Bill 16-24-S allocated $280 from the legislative discretionary fund to Hope Harbor X Denim Day: Inspiring the Next Generation of Volunteers. Hope Harbor is a Bowling Green non-profit supporting people affected by sexual trauma, and Denim Day is an international rape prevention education campaign that asks students, businesses and elected officials to wear jeans as a visible protest against misconceptions about sexual violence. The bill was read a second time on 12 March 2024.

title: WKU Unplugged paid three students to give up their smartphones
body: Bill 34-24-S allocated $886.17 to the WKU Unplugged Scholarship Initiative, an experiment in which three students selected on their application answers surrendered their smartphones to the SGA office and were issued flip phones. A student who lasted the full month without a smartphone was awarded a $200 scholarship. The money covered three flip phones at $286.17 and the three $200 prizes. The bill was read a second time on 28 March 2024.

title: A semester of fundraising for Potter Children's Home
body: Merge into the existing 2024-09-17 entry: the two resolutions were both authored by sophomore senator Jade Ismail and committed SGA to four fundraisers, one in September, two in October and one in December, each carrying a QR code pointing students at a GoFundMe. Resolution 2-24-F set out Soarin' in September at Jump Air Zone on Wednesday 25 September from 8 to 10 p.m., with a $10 entry covering the two hours and socks and every participant signing a safety and liability waiver. title: The second Pink Walk drew survivors to South Lawn
body: SGA's second annual Pink Walk was held on the evening of 17 October 2024, created and hosted by Vice President Donte Reed with WKU Panhellenic, the Interfraternity Council and the National Pan-Hellenic Council, raising money for the Susan G. Komen Breast Cancer Foundation. Students gathered at the Big Red statue in Downing Student Union and walked along Centennial Mall to South Lawn, where SGA served burgers, snacks and drinks. Breast cancer survivors Michelle Denney and Robbin Taylor spoke, along with Tate Sine, whose mother Tonya had spoken at the previous year's walk after her diagnosis in September 2021.

title: A fortnight-long toy drive with Student Activities
body: SGA ran a toy drive with Student Activities from 20 November to 3 December 2024 for the Boys and Girls Club of Bowling Green, taking donations of toys for children aged 3 to 16 at the SGA and Student Activities desks in Downing Student Union. Bill 20-24-F, passed at the meeting of 19 November, put $200 towards additional toys. Donors earned one service hour per toy up to five. The bill was written by sophomore senator Savanna Kurtz, who had worked on the previous year's drive through the Community Relations Committee.

title: SGA Pollooza put a student music festival on South Lawn
body: SGA staged Pollooza, an all-day music festival on South Lawn, on Sunday 13 April 2025, with food trucks, tailgating and a bill of performers drawn entirely from current WKU students. The name folded the word polls into it because the spring election opened that night. Students were told to bring blankets, chairs and tents from about 3 p.m., tailgate rules applied so alcohol was allowed in a cup, five acts were billed from 3 p.m. to 8.30 p.m., and SGA said it would try to stream the final round of the Masters. The Herald's photographers covered the day.

title: Sippin' in September, snowcones and lemonade for Hope Harbor
body: The senate passed a bill on 26 August 2025 clearing a fundraiser called Sippin' in September, run with the local businesses Pelican's Snowcones and Tay Tay's Lemonade in aid of Hope Harbor, the Bowling Green organisation that counsels and supports people affected by sexual harm. Pelican's pledged a fifth of everything raised at the event to Hope Harbor. The bill was written by Jade Ismail, chair of SGA's Action and Opportunity Committee.

title: A hundred pumpkins on South Lawn for Hope Harbor
body: SGA's Action and Opportunity Committee held a campus-wide pumpkin carving contest on South Lawn on Thursday 23 October 2025 from 3 to 5 p.m. as a fundraiser for Hope Harbor. Bill 4-25-F, tabled at its second reading on 9 September before passing at a third reading on 16 September, allocated $320: $250 for a pallet of 100 to 150 pumpkins from Hodge Family Farms, stored in the DSU basement until the day, and a $70 Boo Basket of a heated weighted blanket, candles and donated gifts as the prize. Entry was $10 for up to two carvers, paid straight to the Hope Harbor GoFundMe, and judging was to be done blind by faculty. The Alpha Chi chapter of Alpha Omicron Pi and the Chi Eta chapter of Phi Gamma Delta partnered on the event, covering carving materials and promotion.

title: Toppers Talk About It, a week built around a faculty-student panel
body: A bill passed on 28 October 2025 set up a Mental Health Awareness Week for 3 to 7 November, with a different event each day, among them a day of writing positive affirmations in chalk on the pavements and a day of writing positive messages on sticky notes for other students. The week ended with Flipping the Script, a two-part panel at which faculty from the WKU Counseling Center and the Student Accessibility Resource Center answered questions submitted by students, and then turned the format round so the faculty questioned a group of selected student leaders. The bill was written by Veronica Butler, who told the Herald she wanted the week to raise awareness, reduce stigma and create a supportive campus culture.

title: Judicial Council heard a censure case against a committee chair and dismissed it 7-0
body: The Judicial Council heard a censure case against Senator Jade Ismail, chair of the Action and Opportunity Committee, on 12 November 2025. The complaints included one from members of Alpha Omicron Pi alleging she had treated them poorly when they volunteered at the 23 October pumpkin carving fundraiser she ran, an allegation that she had underspent the sums bills had allocated, which Chief Justice Blake Graham described as undercutting senators' ability to use legislative discretionary funds, and an allegation that she had emailed registered student organisations about a bill before it passed. The council voted 7-0 not to censure, treating most of it as poor communication, and Associate Justice Hannah Hash urged her to keep writing bills.

title: Food for Fines let students pay off a parking ticket in tinned goods
body: The senate passed a bill on 18 November 2025 allowing students to donate food in exchange for exemption from a parking citation, a scheme called Food for Fines run jointly with the WKU Food Pantry and WKU Parking and Transportation Services. Its author, Caden Lucas, chair of the Legislative Operations Committee, argued it would pull far more students into the university food drive at a time when many needed it. At the same meeting a bill from Jade Ismail proposing a raffle in Downing Student Union for Hope Harbor was the only one to fail, senators taking the view that the money should be spent on students on campus.

title: Happy Holidays from the Hill: cards and blankets for a care home
body: Bill 22-25-F allocated $218.61 from the legislative discretionary fund to buy 72 Christmas cards and 60 blankets for residents of Chandler Park Assisted Living. SGA tabled in Downing Student Union on 2 and 3 December 2025 so students could sign the cards, and delivered them with the blankets on 4 December. Students who helped deliver could claim up to three service hours, and senators up to three office hours for attending or tabling. The bill passed its second reading on 18 November 2025.

title: Senators in Christmas pyjamas voted for an open house
body: At the last meeting of the autumn semester on 2 December 2025, senators wearing Christmas pyjamas and Santa hats passed a bill allocating $50.10 to an SGA Winter Welcome on 3 February 2026, an open house at the SGA office meant to raise student attendance at senate meetings. The author, Senator-at-Large Amelia Tucker, told the Herald the house was always open but an open house might bring more people in. The meeting lasted thirty minutes and senators left for the SGA Christmas party at the Cliff Todd Center.

title: Black History Trivia Night with Why Knot Us and Black Women of Western
body: Bill 1-26-S allocated $65 from the legislative discretionary fund towards a Black History Trivia Night held with Why Knot Us and Black Women of Western on 18 February 2026, from 6 to 8 p.m. in DSU room 2123. title: A 200-player Uno tournament to fund student research
body: Bill 3-26-S allocated $209.96 for an Uno tournament fundraiser run with STEMPOWERMENT, passing at its second reading on 24 February 2026. The money hired DSU rooms 3023, 3024 and 3025, merged into one space for three hours at $20 per room per hour, a total of $180, with $29.96 buying four Uno decks. The tournament was capped at 200 players with a $2 entry and paid re-entries at $2 a time, the proceeds supporting student research.

title: F1rstGen staff briefed the senate as it passed a bike rack resolution
body: Cierra Waller and April McCauley of WKU's F1rstGen initiative were guest speakers at the 3 March 2026 meeting, describing the mentorship programme, the first-generation living learning community and the Make It Count service, which gives $250 grants to first-generation students who attend F1rstGen events regularly. Waller said such students were not short of ability but often needed help with unfamiliar university machinery, giving the renaming of the Bursar's Office as the Office of Student Billing and Account Services as an example of the confusion F1rstGen had pushed to clear up. The senate then passed Resolution 3-26-S, which allocates no money but commits SGA to work with Parking and Transportation Services on siting new bike racks and revising the campus bike rack map, prompted by bikes and scooters being locked to railings and stairways.

title: Four more Adirondack chairs for the green spaces
body: Bill 11-26-S allocated $398.98 from the legislative discretionary fund to expand the Adirondack Chair Project, buying two pairs of red Westin Trends chairs at $199.49 a pair. The project had begun in spring 2025, placing chairs at popular spots around campus so students could use the green spaces, and the bill records that students had found the first batch popular and useful enough to justify more. It passed its second reading on 26 March 2026.
